Theorem 16.28, page 306 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider data \(Z^{(N)}=(Y_i,X_i)_{i\le N}\) with \(Y_i=\mathscr{G}(\theta)(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\), \(X_i\) i.i.d. uniform on \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\) and \(\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,I_W)\) i.i.d. and independent of them, where \(\mathscr{G}(\theta)\) is the solution of an evolution equation with initial condition \(\theta:\mathbb{T}^d\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(P^N_{\theta_0}\) be the law of the data under \(\theta_0\). Let \(\Pi\) be the Polson Ročková spike and slab prior on deep ReLU networks \(\theta:\mathbb{T}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) with their width and sparsity hyperpriors and a depth of order \(\log N\), let \(\Theta_N\) be the associated sieve, let \(p\) be the input dimension of the networks in \(\Theta_N\) (\(p=d\) when networks on \([0,1]^d\) approximate the restriction of \(\theta_0\) to \([0,1]^d\), or \(p=2d\) when every network is composed with the periodic embedding \(x\mapsto(\cos2\pi x_1,\sin2\pi x_1,\dots,\cos2\pi x_d,\sin2\pi x_d)\)), and set \[B_N:=1+\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_N}\big(\|\theta\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d)}+\operatorname{Lip}(\theta)\big),\] so that \(\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_N}\|\theta\|_{H^1(\mathbb{T}^d)}\lesssim B_N\). Let \(\theta_0\in C^\alpha(\mathbb{T}^d)\) with \(d/2+1<\alpha<p\). Suppose the forward map satisfies Conditions 2A, 2B and 2E of Nickl (2024) on \(L^\infty\) balls (uniform \(L^\infty\) bounds, \(L^2\) Lipschitz continuity, and the stability estimate \(\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\theta_0)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}\ge c\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{H^{-1}}\)). Then with \(\epsilon_N=N^{-\alpha/(2\alpha+p)}\log^\delta N\), \(\delta>1\), there are \(L,L'>0\) with \[\Pi\big(\theta:\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\theta_0)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}\le L\epsilon_N\mid Z^{(N)}\big)\to1,\qquad\Pi\big(\theta:\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{H^{-1}}\le L\epsilon_N\mid Z^{(N)}\big)\to1,\] in \(P^N_{\theta_0}\) probability, and, by interpolation between \(H^{-1}\) and \(H^1\) along the sieve, \[\Pi\big(\theta:\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{L^2}\le L'(B_N\epsilon_N)^{1/2}\mid Z^{(N)}\big)\to1\] in \(P^N_{\theta_0}\) probability. The third statement is a rate only when \(B_N\epsilon_N\to0\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m3c.tex, label m:thm:PR.




Lemma 16.32, page 310 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. In the linear model \(Y=\Phi\theta+\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,\varsigma^2\operatorname{Id}_N)\), with prior \(\theta\sim N(0,\Sigma_0)\), let \(F=\Phi^\top\Phi/\varsigma^2\) and \(\Sigma_N=(F+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\), and let the one step summary be evaluated at any point \(\bar\theta\): \[S(Y)=\bar\theta+\Sigma_N\Big(\Phi^\top\big(Y-\Phi\bar\theta\big)/\varsigma^2-\Sigma_0^{-1}\bar\theta\Big).\] Then \(S(Y)=\Sigma_N\big(F\theta+\Phi^\top\varepsilon/\varsigma^2\big)\) identically in \(\bar\theta\): the summary is exactly the posterior mean, and in particular does not depend on the linearization point.
Source: source/chapters/ext/m3c.tex, label m:lem:exact.




Theorem 16.33, page 310 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. In the linear model \(Y=\Phi\theta+\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,\varsigma^2\operatorname{Id}_N)\), with prior \(N(0,\Sigma_0)\) on \(D\) retained modes, let \(F=\Phi^\top\Phi/\varsigma^2\), \(\Sigma_N=(F+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\), and for a point \(\bar\theta\) let \(S(Y)=\bar\theta+\Sigma_N(\Phi^\top(Y-\Phi\bar\theta)/\varsigma^2-\Sigma_0^{-1}\bar\theta)\) (which equals the posterior mean). Let the training parameter be drawn from \(q_c=N(\bar\theta,c^2\Sigma_N)\), independent of \(\varepsilon\), so that \(c\) is the localization radius in posterior standard deviations, let \(R=\theta-S(Y)\), and let \(P=\Sigma_N\Sigma_0^{-1}\) be the prior fraction operator, with eigenvalues \(p_1,\dots,p_D\), and \(s_j=1-p_j\). Then \[\mathbb{E}_{q_c}(R)=P\bar\theta,\qquad\operatorname{Var}_{q_c}(R)=c^2P\Sigma_NP^\top+\Sigma_NF\Sigma_N,\] both without further hypotheses. If in addition \(\Sigma_0\) and \(\Phi^\top\Phi\) commute, so that one orthonormal basis diagonalizes \(P\), \(\Sigma_N\) and \(F\) together, then in that basis \(\operatorname{Var}_{q_c}(R)_j=\Sigma_{N,j}(s_j+c^2p_j^2)\). Consequently: (i) under the prior itself, \(\mathbb{E}(R)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(R)=\Sigma_N\), so the identity head is exact; (ii) under \(q_c\) the residual has the mean \(P\bar\theta\), the prior shrinkage of the proposal center, which does not depend on \(c\) and is of first order in the prior fraction; a head that adds the sample mean of the residuals to the center therefore displaces the GBC posterior by \(P\bar\theta\), whereas a head that centers the residuals, or subtracts \(P\bar\theta\) analytically, does not; (iii) with the mean removed, the head misstates the posterior standard deviation in direction \(j\) by the factor \(\sqrt{s_j+c^2p_j^2}\), so the relative error in posterior standard deviations is \[\beta(c)=\frac1D\sum_{j\le D}\Big|\sqrt{s_j+c^2p_j^2}-1\Big|,\] which is \(O(\max_jp_j)\) as \(c\to0\) and grows like \(c\,\frac1D\sum_jp_j\) for large \(c\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m3c.tex, label m:thm:locbias.




Corollary 16.37, page 315 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. In the linear model \(Y=\Phi\theta+\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,\varsigma^2\operatorname{Id}_N)\), with prior \(N(0,\Sigma_0)\), let \(F=\Phi^\top\Phi/\varsigma^2\), \(\Sigma_N=(F+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\), and suppose \(\Sigma_0\) and \(\Phi^\top\Phi\) commute; let \(P=\Sigma_N\Sigma_0^{-1}\), with eigenvalues \(p_j\), \(s_j=1-p_j\), and for a preliminary estimate \(\bar\theta_N\) let \(S(Y)=\bar\theta_N+\Sigma_N(\Phi^\top(Y-\Phi\bar\theta_N)/\varsigma^2-\Sigma_0^{-1}\bar\theta_N)\), the posterior mean, so that the exact posterior is \(\Pi_N=N(S(Y),\Sigma_N)\). Consider the localized GBC generator: training parameters \(\theta^{(m)}\sim q_c=N(\bar\theta_N,c^2\Sigma_N)\), \(m\le M\), with simulated data \(Y^{(m)}\); an identity head with the residuals \(\theta^{(m)}-S(Y^{(m)})\) centered at their sample mean, whitened by the sample covariance of the centered residuals rescaled by \((s_j+c^2p_j^2)^{-1/2}\) in the eigenbasis of \(P\), and centered at \(S(Y)\) for the observed data, with no residual mean added to the center, no affine head and no importance weighting back to the prior; let \(\widehat\Pi_N\) be the law it produces. Then: (i) (exactness in population) for every \(c>0\) and every center \(\bar\theta_N\), the law the head produces at the observed data is exactly the posterior \(N(S(Y),\Sigma_N)\): localization contributes no bias at all; (ii) (finite \(M\)) with \(M=M_N\) simulations and \(J=J_N\) retained modes, the rescaled sample covariance of the centered residuals equals \(\Sigma_N^{1/2}(\operatorname{Id}+\Delta_M)\Sigma_N^{1/2}\), where \(\|\Delta_M\|_{op}=O_P(\sqrt{J_N/M_N}+J_N/M_N)\) does not depend on \(c\); hence, when \(\Sigma_{N,j}\lesssim\lambda_j/N\) on the retained modes (\(\lambda_j\) the Laplace eigenvalues), as for the heat and Stokes equations, and \(k>d/2\), \(\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-k-2}}(\widehat\Pi_N,\Pi_N)=O_P\big(N^{-1/2}(\sqrt{J_N/M_N}+J_N/M_N)\big)\), the distance being the Wasserstein distance of order one for the norm \(\|x\|^2=\sum_j\lambda_j^{-k-2}x_j^2\) on the coefficients in the first \(J\) Laplace modes, so the accuracy condition (G1) \(\sqrt N\,\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-k-2}}(\widehat\Pi_N,\Pi_N)\to0\) holds whenever \(J_N/M_N\to0\), at every radius, and the condition (G2) (exponentially small mass off the localization set and moments of every order) holds whenever the exact posterior \(N(S(Y),\Sigma_N)\) satisfies its first clause; (iii) consequently the transfer theorem (catalog entry bvm_for_gbc) applies verbatim to this algorithm, its accuracy assumption being discharged.
Source: source/chapters/ext/m3c.tex, label m:cor:locG.




Lemma 16.41, page 319 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\) with \(X\) uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\), let \((e_j)\) be the Laplace eigenbasis of \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) (the torus), \(P_J\) the orthogonal projection onto \(\operatorname{span}\{e_j:j\le J\}\cong\mathbb{R}^J\) and \(Q_J=\operatorname{Id}-P_J\). Let \(\mathbb{I}_{\bar\vartheta}\) be the linearization at a point \(\bar\vartheta\) of the solution map \(\theta\mapsto u_\theta\), with values in \(\mathbb{R}^{d_W}\) valued functions on \(\mathcal{X}\), let \(\mathcal{D}=\operatorname{diag}(1/\iota_j)\) be the heat (or Stokes) information diagonal, and define \(K'_{\bar\vartheta}\) by \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\bar\vartheta}=T^{-1}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\mathbb{I}^*_{\bar\vartheta}\mathbb{I}_{\bar\vartheta}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\), that is \(\langle f,(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\bar\vartheta})g\rangle=\mathbb{E}\langle(\mathbb{I}_{\bar\vartheta}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}f)(X),(\mathbb{I}_{\bar\vartheta}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}g)(X)\rangle_W\). Let \(\mathcal{A}=\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\bar\vartheta}\) be bounded on \(\ell^2\) with \(\mathcal{A}\succeq a\operatorname{Id}\) for some \(a>0\), and write \(B_J=P_J\mathcal{A}^{-1}P_J\). Let the whitened weights be the \(J\times d_W\) matrix \(\phi(x)\) defined by \(\phi(x)^\top v=(\mathbb{I}_{\bar\vartheta}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}P_J\mathcal{A}^{-1}v)(x)\) for \(v\in\mathbb{R}^J\) (equivalently, row \(j\) is \(\iota_j^{1/2}\) times the weight function \(\mathbb{I}_{\bar\vartheta}P_J(T(\mathbb{I}^*_{\bar\vartheta}\mathbb{I}_{\bar\vartheta})^{-1}e_j)\) of the one step summary linearized at \(\bar\vartheta\)), and \(G_\phi=\mathbb{E}\,\phi(X)\phi(X)^\top\) their Gram matrix. Then \[G_\phi=B_J+B_JP_J\mathcal{A}Q_J(Q_J\mathcal{A}Q_J)^{-1}Q_J\mathcal{A}P_JB_J,\] so that \(G_\phi\succeq B_J\succeq\|\mathcal{A}\|^{-1}_{op}\operatorname{Id}\) and \(\|G_\phi-B_J\|_{op}\le a^{-3}\|K'_{\bar\vartheta}Q_J\|^2_{op}\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m3c.tex, label m:lem:u2pgram.




Proposition 16.42, page 319 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\), \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) the torus, with \(X\) uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\), and let \(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\) be the linearization at \(\vartheta\) of the solution map \(\theta\mapsto u_\theta\), whose values are \(\mathbb{R}^{d_W}\) valued functions on \(\mathcal{X}\). Let \(\mathcal{D}=\operatorname{diag}(1/\iota_j)\) be the heat (or Stokes) information diagonal, \(\iota_j=(1-e^{-2\nu\lambda_jT})/(2\nu\lambda_jT)\) with \(\lambda_j\) the Laplace eigenvalues, \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_\vartheta=T^{-1}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\mathbb{I}^*_\vartheta\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\), and \(P_J\) the projection onto the first \(J\) eigenfunctions \(e_1,\dots,e_J\). Fix a linearization point \(\bar\vartheta\) determined by the data \(Z^{(N)}\) at which \(\mathcal{A}=\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\bar\vartheta}\) is bounded and invertible, let \(\phi(x)\) be the \(J\times d_W\) matrix with \(\phi(x)^\top v=(\mathbb{I}_{\bar\vartheta}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}P_J\mathcal{A}^{-1}v)(x)\) for \(v\in\mathbb{R}^J\) (rows \(\phi_j(x)^\top\)), \(G_\phi=\mathbb{E}\,\phi(X)\phi(X)^\top\) and \(b_J=\operatorname{ess\,sup}_x\|\phi(x)\|^2_{op}\). Let each simulated data set \(Z^{(m)}\) be drawn at a training parameter \(\theta^{(m)}\) with its own design points \(X^{(m)}_i\), i.i.d. uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\), and its own noise \(\varepsilon^{(m)}_i\sim N(0,I_W)\), independent of each other and of \(\theta^{(m)}\), let the training summary be the one step summary linearized once at \(\bar\vartheta\) with the population information and no prior term, \(\hat S^{(m)}_{N,j}=\langle e_j,\bar\vartheta\rangle+N^{-1}\sum_{i\le N}\langle\iota_j^{-1/2}\phi_j(X^{(m)}_i),Y^{(m)}_i-u_{\bar\vartheta}(X^{(m)}_i)\rangle_W\) for \(j\le J\), and let \(W^{(m)}=\mathcal{D}^{-1/2}\sqrt N(P_J\theta^{(m)}-\hat S^{(m)}_N)\) be the whitened residual. Let the training parameters have any law given \(Z^{(N)}\), and write \(\|\chi\|_{\psi_2\mid Z^{(N)}}=\inf\{K>0:\mathbb{E}[e^{\chi^2/K^2}\mid Z^{(N)}]\le2\}\). Then for every \(N\), every \(J\) and every unit vector \(v\in\mathbb{R}^J\) \[\big\|\langle v,W^{(m)}\rangle\big\|^2_{\psi_2\mid Z^{(N)}}\ge2\operatorname{ess\,sup}_x\|\phi(x)^\top v\|^2_W,\qquad\sup_{\|u\|_2=1}\big\|\langle u,W^{(m)}\rangle\big\|^2_{\psi_2\mid Z^{(N)}}\ge2b_J\ge\frac{2\,\mathrm{tr}\,G_\phi}{d_W}.\] If \(\mathcal{A}\) is bounded and \(\mathcal{A}\succeq a\operatorname{Id}\) for some \(a>0\), then \(\mathrm{tr}\,G_\phi\ge J\|\mathcal{A}\|^{-1}_{op}\). For the heat and Stokes equations, observed from time zero, \(G_\phi=\operatorname{Id}_J\) and \(\|\langle e_J,W^{(m)}\rangle\|^2_{\psi_2\mid Z^{(N)}}\ge2\|e_J\|^2_{L^\infty}/\iota_J\ge2/\iota_J\), which grows like \(\lambda_J\); for the real trigonometric basis the bound is \(4/\iota_J\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m3c.tex, label m:prop:u2pfalse.




Theorem 16.43, page 320 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Setting. Data \(Z^{(N)}\): \(Y_i=u_\theta(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\), \(i\le N\), \(X_i\) i.i.d. uniform on \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\), \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) the torus, \(\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,I_W)\) in \(\mathbb{R}^{d_W}\); \((e_j)\) the Laplace eigenbasis with eigenvalues \(\lambda_j\); \(\theta_0\) the truth and \(P^N_{\theta_0}\) the law of the data; Nickl’s rescaled Gaussian series prior with \(\delta_N=N^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), and \(\tilde\delta_N(\xi)=\delta_N^{(\bar\gamma-\xi)/(\bar\gamma+1)}\) with \(\bar\gamma\) the Sobolev index of the localization ball. Let \(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\) be the linearization of \(\theta\mapsto u_\theta\) at \(\vartheta\), \(\mathcal{D}=\operatorname{diag}(1/\iota_j)\) the heat (or Stokes) information diagonal with \(\iota_j=(1-e^{-2\nu\lambda_jT})/(2\nu\lambda_jT)\), \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_\vartheta=T^{-1}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\mathbb{I}^*_\vartheta\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\), \(P_J\) the projection onto the first \(J\) modes and \(\operatorname{Id}+\Xi=P_J(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\theta_0})^{-1}P_J\). Let \(\bar\theta_N\) be a preliminary estimate computed from half of the sample with \(\|\bar\theta_N-\theta_0\|_{H^\xi}=O_P(\tilde\delta_N(\xi))\) for \(0\le\xi\le\bar\gamma\), and let \(J=J_N\asymp N^{d/(2\gamma+d)}\). Let the training parameters be \[\theta^{(m)}=\bar\theta_N+N^{-1/2}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\mathcal{V}_N^{1/2}\xi^{(m)},\qquad m\le M,\] where \(\mathcal{V}_N\) is a positive semidefinite \(J\times J\) matrix determined by \(Z^{(N)}\) with \(\|\mathcal{V}_N\|_{op}=O_P(1)\), and the \(\xi^{(m)}\) are i.i.d. standard normal on \(\mathbb{R}^J\) given \(Z^{(N)}\), conditioned on \(\|\xi^{(m)}\|_2^2\le4J\) when the forward map is nonlinear. Each simulated data set has its own uniform design \(X^{(m)}_i\) and noise \(\varepsilon^{(m)}_i\). With \(\phi(x)\) the \(J\times d_W\) matrix given by \(\phi(x)^\top v=(\mathbb{I}_{\bar\theta_N}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}P_J(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\bar\theta_N})^{-1}v)(x)\), rows \(\phi_j(x)^\top\), the training summary is \(\hat S^{(m)}_{N,j}=\langle e_j,\bar\theta_N\rangle+N^{-1}\sum_{i\le N}\langle\iota_j^{-1/2}\phi_j(X^{(m)}_i),Y^{(m)}_i-u_{\bar\theta_N}(X^{(m)}_i)\rangle_W\), \(j\le J\) (linearized once at \(\bar\theta_N\), population information, no prior term), and the whitened residuals are \(W^{(m)}=\mathcal{D}^{-1/2}\sqrt N(P_J\theta^{(m)}-\hat S^{(m)}_N)\), used uncentered and unrescaled by the identity skip Gaussian head generator (catalog entry bernstein_von_mises_for_the_identity_skip_quantile_generator). Assumption (U2’) means: \(W^{(m)}=W^{(m)}_{g}+W^{(m)}_{r}\) with pairs i.i.d. given \(Z^{(N)}\), \(\varkappa_N=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|\langle v,W^{(m)}_{g}\rangle\|_{\psi_2\mid Z^{(N)}}=O_P(1)\), where \(\|\chi\|_{\psi_2\mid Z^{(N)}}=\inf\{K>0:\mathbb{E}[e^{\chi^2/K^2}\mid Z^{(N)}]\le2\}\), and, in \(P^N_{\theta_0}\) probability, \(\mathbb{E}[\|W^{(m)}_{r}\|^2_2\mid Z^{(N)}]\to0\) and \(\|\mathbb{E}[W^{(m)}_{g}W^{(m)\top}_{g}\mid Z^{(N)}]-(\operatorname{Id}+\Xi)\|_{op}\to0\).
Conditions on the linearization, with a constant \(a_\star>0\) and, for every \(B>0\), constants \(L_\star\) and \(C_\infty\) that may depend on \(B\), required for all \(\vartheta\) with \(\|\vartheta\|_{H^{\bar\gamma}}\le B\): (I1) \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\theta_0}\) is bounded on \(\ell^2\), \(K'_{\theta_0}\) is compact and \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\theta_0}\succeq a_\star\operatorname{Id}\); (I2) \(\|(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta-\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0})\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\|_{\ell^2\to L^2}\le L_\star\|\vartheta-\theta_0\|_{H^\zeta}\), where \(\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell^2\to L^2}=\sup_{\|g\|_2\le1}(\mathbb{E}\|(\mathcal{T}g)(X)\|^2_W)^{1/2}\) with \(X\) uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\); (I3) \(\|\mathbb{I}_\vartheta h\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})}\le C_\infty\|h\|_{H^\zeta}\) for all \(h\in H^\zeta\).
Then: (a) for the heat and Stokes equations, observed from time zero, with \(\gamma>d+2\), Assumption (U2’) holds with \(\Xi=0\), \(\varkappa_N\le4/\sqrt3\) and \(W^{(m)}_{g}=-\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{B}_m}N^{-1/2}\sum_i\phi(X^{(m)}_i)\varepsilon^{(m)}_i\), where \(\mathcal{B}_m=\{\|\hat G^{(m)}_\phi-\operatorname{Id}\|_{op}\le1\}\) and \(\hat G^{(m)}_\phi=N^{-1}\sum_{i\le N}\phi(X^{(m)}_i)\phi(X^{(m)}_i)^\top\); (b) for a nonlinear forward map, Assumption (U2’) holds under Conditions 1 and 2 of Nickl (2024) with integer \(\gamma>\max(3\zeta+3d/2+2,\eta_0)\) and \(k>\max(\zeta+5d/2,\eta_0)\) (\(\zeta>d/2\) the index of Condition 2D), \(\bar\gamma<\gamma-1\), \(\sqrt N\,\tilde\delta_N(0)\tilde\delta_N(\zeta)\to0\), and (I1) to (I3); (c) let \(\Sigma_0\) be positive definite, \(\Sigma_N=(F_{\bar\theta_N}+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\) with \(F_{\bar\theta_N}\) the realized information on \(J\) modes, and \(a_\star=1\) in case (a); under the hypotheses of (a) or (b), with probability tending to one \(N^{-1}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}F_{\bar\theta_N}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\succeq(a_\star/12)\operatorname{Id}\), and then \(\mathcal{V}_N=c^2N\mathcal{D}^{-1/2}\Sigma_N\mathcal{D}^{-1/2}\) has \(\|\mathcal{V}_N\|_{op}\le12c^2/a_\star\).

Lemma 16.44, page 324 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) be the torus with \(d\le3\), \(T>0\), \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\), and let \(u_\vartheta\) solve \(\partial_tu-\Delta u=f(u)\), \(u(0)=\vartheta\), with \(f\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R})\) (the setting of Theorem 1 of Nickl (2024), with integer \(\gamma>2+3d\)), let \(\theta_0\in C^\infty\) and \(K_f=\sup|f'|\), and let \(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta h\) be the solution \(U\) of \(\partial_tU=\Delta U+f'(u_\vartheta)U\), \(U(0)=h\). Let \(\mathcal{D}=\operatorname{diag}(1/\iota_j)\) be the heat information diagonal in the Laplace eigenbasis, \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_\vartheta=T^{-1}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\mathbb{I}^*_\vartheta\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\), and \(\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell^2\to L^2}=\sup_{\|g\|_2\le1}(\mathbb{E}|(\mathcal{T}g)(X)|^2)^{1/2}\) with \(X\) uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\). Consider the conditions, with a constant \(a_\star>0\) and, for every \(B>0\), constants \(L_\star\), \(C_\infty\), \(C_Q\) that may depend on \(B\), for all \(\vartheta,\vartheta'\) with \(\|\vartheta\|_{H^{\bar\gamma}},\|\vartheta'\|_{H^{\bar\gamma}}\le B\): (I1) \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\theta_0}\) is bounded on \(\ell^2\), \(K'_{\theta_0}\) is compact and \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\theta_0}\succeq a_\star\operatorname{Id}\); (I2) \(\|(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta-\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0})\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\|_{\ell^2\to L^2}\le L_\star\|\vartheta-\theta_0\|_{H^\zeta}\); (I3) \(\|\mathbb{I}_\vartheta h\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})}\le C_\infty\|h\|_{H^\zeta}\) for all \(h\in H^\zeta\); (I4) \(\|u_{\vartheta'}-u_\vartheta-\mathbb{I}_\vartheta[\vartheta'-\vartheta]\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})}\le C_Q\|\vartheta'-\vartheta\|^2_{H^\zeta}\). Then (I1) to (I4) hold for every \(\zeta>d/2\) and every \(\bar\gamma>\max(1,\zeta)\), and \(\|\operatorname{Id}+K'_\vartheta\|_{op}\) is bounded by a constant that depends only on \(K_f\) and \(T\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m3c.tex, label m:lem:rdlin.




Lemma 16.45, page 325 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider the incompressible Navier Stokes equations on the two dimensional torus, as in Konen and Nickl (2026), with forcing \(f\in\dot H^{1}_\diamond\) and initial condition \(\theta_0\in\dot H^{2}_\diamond\), where \(\dot H^{s}_\diamond\) is the Sobolev space of order \(s\) of divergence free, mean zero vector fields; let \(u_\vartheta\) be the solution with initial condition \(\vartheta\), \(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\) the linearization of \(\vartheta\mapsto u_\vartheta\) (the solution of the equation linearized at \(u_\vartheta\)), \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^2\), \(\mathcal{D}=\operatorname{diag}(1/\iota_j)\) the Stokes information diagonal and \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_\vartheta=T^{-1}\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\mathbb{I}^*_\vartheta\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\). Consider the conditions, with a constant \(a_\star>0\) and, for every \(B>0\), constants \(L_\star\), \(C_\infty\), \(C_Q\) that may depend on \(B\), for all \(\vartheta,\vartheta'\) with \(\|\vartheta\|_{H^{\bar\gamma}},\|\vartheta'\|_{H^{\bar\gamma}}\le B\): (I1) \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\theta_0}\) is bounded on \(\ell^2\), \(K'_{\theta_0}\) is compact and \(\operatorname{Id}+K'_{\theta_0}\succeq a_\star\operatorname{Id}\); (I2) \(\|(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta-\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0})\mathcal{D}^{1/2}\|_{\ell^2\to L^2}\le L_\star\|\vartheta-\theta_0\|_{H^\zeta}\), with \(\|\mathcal{T}\|_{\ell^2\to L^2}=\sup_{\|g\|_2\le1}(\mathbb{E}\|(\mathcal{T}g)(X)\|^2)^{1/2}\) for \(X\) uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\); (I3) \(\|\mathbb{I}_\vartheta h\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})}\le C_\infty\|h\|_{H^\zeta}\) for all \(h\in H^\zeta\); (I4) \(\|u_{\vartheta'}-u_\vartheta-\mathbb{I}_\vartheta[\vartheta'-\vartheta]\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})}\le C_Q\|\vartheta'-\vartheta\|^2_{H^\zeta}\). Then (I2) to (I4) hold with \(\zeta=2\) for every \(\bar\gamma\ge2\). If moreover \(f,\theta_0\in\dot H^{\infty}_\diamond\), as in Theorem 2.11 of Konen and Nickl (2026), then, with (I1), which the book proves for Navier Stokes by the Fredholm alternative, and with Condition 2C (linearization with quadratic remainder) from their Proposition 3.8(iii), every hypothesis on the forward map of part (b) of the theorem on the whitened residual assumption under a localized proposal (catalog entry whitened_residual_assumption_under_a_localized_proposal) holds, with their Condition 2.12 in place of Condition 2 of Nickl (2024) and \(\gamma=\alpha>12>3\zeta+3d/2+2\).

Proposition 16.47, page 327 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Use the setting of the theorem on the whitened residual assumption under a localized proposal (catalog entry whitened_residual_assumption_under_a_localized_proposal): data \(Y_i=u_\theta(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\) on \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\) with the observed design \((X_i)_{i\le N}\), a preliminary estimate \(\bar\theta_N\), \(J=J_N\) retained modes with projection \(P_J\), the linearization \(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\) of \(\theta\mapsto u_\theta\) and the heat (or Stokes) information diagonal \(\mathcal{D}\). Let \(\Sigma_0\) be positive definite, \(\Sigma_N=(F_{\bar\theta_N}+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\) with \(F_{\bar\theta_N}\) the realized information on \(J\) modes, \(c>0\), and \(\theta^{(m)}=\bar\theta_N+c\Sigma_N^{1/2}\xi^{(m)}\), \(m\le M\), with the \(\xi^{(m)}\) i.i.d. standard normal on \(\mathbb{R}^J\) given the data, conditioned on \(\|\xi^{(m)}\|^2_2\le4J\). Let the simulated data sets reuse the observed design and draw fresh noise, and let \(S^{(m)}\) be their regularized one step summaries on \(J\) modes formed at \(\bar\theta_N\) with this \(\Sigma_N\), \(S^{(m)}=\bar\theta_N+\Sigma_N\big(\mathbb{I}^*_{\bar\theta_N}\big[\sum_ir^{(m)}_i\delta_{X_i}\big]-\Sigma_0^{-1}\bar\theta_N\big)\) with residuals \(r^{(m)}_i=Y^{(m)}_i-u_{\bar\theta_N}(X_i)\), and \(S(Y)\) the same summary of the observed data. Let \(Q\) be the rescaling of the localized GBC algorithm, multiplication by \((s_j+c^2p_j^2)^{-1/2}\) in the eigenbasis of \(P=\Sigma_N\Sigma_0^{-1}\), whose eigenvalues are \(p_j\), with \(s_j=1-p_j\). Then \[\Sigma_N^{-1/2}Q\big(P_J\theta^{(m)}-S^{(m)}\big)=\mu_N+W^{(m)}_{g}+W^{(m)}_{r}\] with \(\mu_N\) determined by \(Z^{(N)}\), and under the hypotheses of part (b) of that theorem (Conditions 1 and 2 of Nickl (2024) with integer \(\gamma>\max(3\zeta+3d/2+2,\eta_0)\) and \(k>\max(\zeta+5d/2,\eta_0)\), \(\bar\gamma<\gamma-1\), \(\sqrt N\,\tilde\delta_N(0)\tilde\delta_N(\zeta)\to0\), and the linearization conditions (I1) to (I3)) and the quadratic remainder condition (I4) \(\|u_{\vartheta'}-u_\vartheta-\mathbb{I}_\vartheta[\vartheta'-\vartheta]\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})}\le C_Q\|\vartheta'-\vartheta\|^2_{H^\zeta}\) on \(H^{\bar\gamma}\) balls, the pairs \((W^{(m)}_{g},W^{(m)}_{r})\) satisfy Assumption (U2’) with \(\operatorname{Id}\) in place of \(\operatorname{Id}+\Xi\) (i.i.d. given the data, \(\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|\langle v,W^{(m)}_{g}\rangle\|_{\psi_2\mid Z^{(N)}}=O_P(1)\), \(\mathbb{E}[\|W^{(m)}_{r}\|^2_2\mid Z^{(N)}]\to0\) and \(\|\mathbb{E}[W^{(m)}_{g}W^{(m)\top}_{g}\mid Z^{(N)}]-\operatorname{Id}\|_{op}\to0\) in probability), and \(\max_m\|W^{(m)}_{r}\|_2\to0\) in probability. If \(J_N/M_N\to0\), the head of the localized GBC algorithm, centered at \(S(Y)\), produces a law \(\widehat\Pi_N\) with \(\sqrt N\,\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-k-2}}\big(\widehat\Pi_N,N(S(Y),\Sigma_N)\big)\to0\) in probability.

Proposition 17.1, page 332 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(e_1,\dots,e_D\) be real orthonormal eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on \(\mathbb{T}^d\), \(-\Delta e_j=\lambda_je_j\), with \(\|e_j\|_\infty\le\sqrt2\) for all \(j\le D\). Consider the heat equation \(\partial_tu=\nu\Delta u\) with \(\nu>0\) and initial condition \(\theta=\sum_{j\le D}\theta_je_j\), observed at \(N\) independent points \((t_i,x_i)\) drawn uniformly from \([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\) with unit variance Gaussian noise, so that \(Y=\Phi\theta+\varepsilon\) with design matrix \(\Phi_{ij}=e^{-\nu\lambda_jt_i}e_j(x_i)\), \(i\le N\), \(j\le D\). Put \(\iota_j=\frac1T\int_0^Te^{-2\nu\lambda_jt}\,\mathrm{d}t=(1-e^{-2\nu\lambda_jT})/(2\nu\lambda_jT)\) and suppose \(N\ge D\log D\). Then, with the absolute constant \(c=12\), \(\|N^{-1}\Phi^\top\Phi-\operatorname{diag}(\iota_j)\|_{op}\le c\sqrt{D\log D/N}\) with probability at least \(1-D^{-1}\). Consequently, on the same event, if \(c\sqrt{D\log D/N}<\min_j\iota_j\) then, for a Gaussian prior \(N(0,\Sigma_0)\) on \(\theta\) with \(\Sigma_0\) positive definite, the exact posterior covariance \(V_N=(\Phi^\top\Phi+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\) and its Bernstein von Mises prediction \(\bar V_N=(N\operatorname{diag}(\iota_j)+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\) satisfy \(\|NV_N-N\bar V_N\|_{op}\le c\sqrt{D\log D/N}\,\big/\,\big(\min_j\iota_j\,(\min_j\iota_j-c\sqrt{D\log D/N})\big)\).

Proposition 17.5, page 356 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\kappa\in\mathbb{R}\), \(d\le2\), and let \(u\) solve the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \(i\partial_tu+\Delta u=\kappa|u|^2u\) on \(\mathbb{T}^d\) with the constant real initial condition \(\theta_0=a\), so that \(u_0(t)=a\,e^{-i\kappa a^2t}\). The linearization at \(u_0\) is \(i\partial_tU+\Delta U=\kappa(2|u_0|^2U+u_0^2\bar U)\), \(U(0)=h\). Writing \(U=e^{-i\kappa a^2t}(\phi+i\psi)\) with \(\phi,\psi\) real, the Fourier coefficients \((\phi_p,\psi_p)\) at the wave vector \(p=2\pi k\), \(k\in\mathbb{Z}^d\), satisfy \(\frac{d}{dt}(\phi_p,\psi_p)^\top=A_p(\phi_p,\psi_p)^\top\) with \(A_p=\begin{pmatrix}0&|p|^2\\-(|p|^2+2\kappa a^2)&0\end{pmatrix}\), where \(|p|^2=4\pi^2|k|^2\) is the eigenvalue of \(-\Delta\) at that mode. Put \(\omega_p^2=|p|^2(|p|^2+2\kappa a^2)\) (the Bogoliubov dispersion relation) and let \(M_p(t)=e^{tA_p}\) be the propagator. Then, with \((\mathrm{Re}\,U,\mathrm{Im}\,U)\) observed at points uniform on \([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\), the information operator of the linearized model (the linearization composed with its adjoint in unnormalized \(L^2([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d)\)) is block diagonal over Fourier modes with \(2\times2\) blocks \(\Theta_p(T)=\int_0^TM_p(t)^\top M_p(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\) acting on \((\phi_p(0),\psi_p(0))\). In the stable case \(\omega_p^2>0\) (which excludes the block \(p=0\), where \(\omega_0=0\)), with \(\omega=\omega_p\) and \(r=\omega_p/|p|^2=(1+2\kappa a^2/|p|^2)^{1/2}\): \(M_p(t)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\omega t&r^{-1}\sin\omega t\\-r\sin\omega t&\cos\omega t\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\Theta_p(T)=\frac T2\begin{pmatrix}1+r^2&0\\0&1+r^{-2}\end{pmatrix}+\frac{\sin2\omega T}{4\omega}\begin{pmatrix}1-r^2&0\\0&1-r^{-2}\end{pmatrix}+\frac{\sin^2\omega T}{2\omega}(r^{-1}-r)\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), so that \(\Theta_p(T)=T\operatorname{Id}+O(\kappa a^2T/|p|^2)+O(|p|^{-2})\) as \(|p|\to\infty\), and \(\det\Theta_p(T)\ge T^2\) for every \(p\) and every \(T>0\). In the unstable case \(\omega_p^2<0\) (which happens for \(\kappa<0\) and \(|p|^2<2|\kappa|a^2\), the modulational or Benjamin Feir instability), with \(\gamma=|\omega_p|\) and \(\rho=\gamma/|p|^2\): \(M_p(t)=\begin{pmatrix}\cosh\gamma t&\rho^{-1}\sinh\gamma t\\\rho\sinh\gamma t&\cosh\gamma t\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\Theta_p(T)=\frac T2\begin{pmatrix}1-\rho^2&0\\0&1-\rho^{-2}\end{pmatrix}+\frac{\sinh2\gamma T}{4\gamma}\begin{pmatrix}1+\rho^2&0\\0&1+\rho^{-2}\end{pmatrix}+\frac{\sinh^2\gamma T}{2\gamma}(\rho+\rho^{-1})\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\); as \(\gamma T\to\infty\) the largest eigenvalue of \(\Theta_p(T)\) is asymptotic to \((\rho+\rho^{-1})^2e^{2\gamma T}/(8\gamma)\) and its smallest eigenvalue tends to \(1/(2\gamma)\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m4d.tex, label m:prop:bog.




Lemma 17.6, page 359 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\kappa\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(a\in\mathbb{R}\), and consider the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \(i\partial_tu+\Delta u=\kappa|u|^2u\) on \(\mathbb{T}^d\) linearized about the constant solution \(u_0(t)=a\,e^{-i\kappa a^2t}\). For the wave vector \(p=2\pi k\), \(k\in\mathbb{Z}^d\), let \(A_p=\begin{pmatrix}0&|p|^2\\-(|p|^2+2\kappa a^2)&0\end{pmatrix}\), \(M_p(t)=e^{tA_p}\), \(\omega_p^2=|p|^2(|p|^2+2\kappa a^2)\) and \(\Theta_p(T)=\int_0^TM_p(t)^\top M_p(t)\,\mathrm{d}t\) (the \(2\times2\) block of the information operator of the linearization over \([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\)). Write \(\omega=\omega_p\) and \(r=r_p=\omega_p/|p|^2\) in the elliptic case \(\omega_p^2>0\), and \(\gamma=\gamma_p=|\omega_p|\) and \(\rho=\rho_p=\gamma_p/|p|^2\) in the hyperbolic case \(\omega_p^2<0\). Then for every \(T>0\): (i) \(\det M_p(t)=1\) for all \(t\), and consequently \(\det\Theta_p(T)\ge T^2\) for every \(p\) and every \(T>0\), with no restriction on \(\omega_pT\). (ii) For \(p\ne0\) in the elliptic case, \(\det\Theta_p(T)=T^2+\frac{(r-r^{-1})^2}{4}\big(T^2-\frac{\sin^2\omega T}{\omega^2}\big)\); in the hyperbolic case, \(\det\Theta_p(T)=T^2+\frac{(\rho+\rho^{-1})^2}{4}\big(\gamma^{-2}\sinh^2\gamma T-T^2\big)\). At \(p=0\), \(\Theta_0(T)=T\begin{pmatrix}1+\frac43s^2&-s\\-s&1\end{pmatrix}\) with \(s=\kappa a^2T\), so that \(\det\Theta_0(T)=T^2(1+\frac13s^2)\). (iii) In the elliptic case, \(\mathrm{tr}\,\Theta_p(T)=2T+(r-r^{-1})^2\int_0^T\sin^2\omega t\,\mathrm{d}t\le T(r^2+r^{-2})\), and \(\mathrm{tr}\,\Theta_0(T)=T(2+\frac43s^2)\). (iv) In the elliptic case, \(\lambda_{\min}(\Theta_p(T))\ge T/(r_p^2+r_p^{-2})\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\Theta_0(T))\ge T/4\). If \(r_p\ge1\) this implies \(\lambda_{\min}\ge T/(1+r_p^2)\); if \(r_p<1\) the bound \(T/(1+r_p^2)\) is false in general, so \(r_p^2+r_p^{-2}\) cannot be replaced by \(1+r_p^2\). (v) In the defocusing case \(\kappa>0\), \(1<r_p^2\le1+2\kappa a^2/\lambda_1\) for \(p\ne0\), where \(\lambda_1=4\pi^2\) is the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of \(-\Delta\) on \(\mathbb{T}^d\), and \(\inf_p\lambda_{\min}(\Theta_p(T))\ge\dfrac{T\lambda_1}{4(\lambda_1+\kappa a^2)}\) and \(\sup_{p\ne0}\lambda_{\max}(\Theta_p(T))\le\dfrac{2T(\lambda_1+\kappa a^2)}{\lambda_1}\). (vi) In the focusing band \(\omega_p^2<0\), as \(\gamma_pT\to\infty\), \(\lambda_{\max}(\Theta_p(T))\sim\mathrm{tr}\,\Theta_p(T)\sim(\rho_p+\rho_p^{-1})^2e^{2\gamma_pT}/(8\gamma_p)\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(\Theta_p(T))=\det\Theta_p(T)/\lambda_{\max}(\Theta_p(T))\to1/(2\gamma_p)\); the bound \(\lambda_{\min}\ge T^2/\mathrm{tr}\,\Theta_p(T)\) still holds but is exponentially small in \(\gamma_pT\), and the condition number satisfies \(\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}\sim\frac14(\rho_p+\rho_p^{-1})^2e^{2\gamma_pT}\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m4d.tex, label m:lem:bogmin.




Corollary 17.7, page 362 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\kappa>0\) (defocusing), \(d\le2\) and \(a\in\mathbb{R}\), let \(\Omega=\mathbb{T}^d\) and \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\), and let \(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}\) be the linearization at the plane wave \(u_0(t)=a\,e^{-i\kappa a^2t}\) (initial condition \(\theta_0=a\)) of the solution map of \(i\partial_tu+\Delta u=\kappa|u|^2u\), namely \(h\mapsto U\) with \(i\partial_tU+\Delta U=\kappa(2|u_0|^2U+u_0^2\bar U)\), \(U(0)=h\), with adjoint \(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}^*\) taken with respect to unnormalized \(L^2(\mathcal{X})\). Let \(\lambda_1=4\pi^2\) be the smallest nonzero eigenvalue of \(-\Delta\) and set \(c_\star^2=\dfrac{T\lambda_1}{4(\lambda_1+\kappa a^2)}\) and \(C_\star^2=\max\Big\{\dfrac{2T(\lambda_1+\kappa a^2)}{\lambda_1},\ T\big(2+\tfrac43\kappa^2a^4T^2\big)\Big\}\). Then for every \(h\in L^2(\mathbb{T}^d;\mathbb{C})\), \(c_\star^2\|h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\le\|\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}h\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2=\langle h,\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}^*\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}h\rangle\le C_\star^2\|h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\), and consequently: (a) \(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}^*\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}\) is a homeomorphism of \(H^\eta(\mathbb{T}^d)\) for every \(\eta\in\mathbb{R}\), with the explicit constants \(c_\star^2,C_\star^2\); this is the analogue of Nickl’s Condition 2F (invertibility of the information operator: \(\Delta\mathbb{I}^*\mathbb{I}\) is a homeomorphism of \(H^\eta_0\) for \(\eta\ge\eta_0\)) without the factor \(\Delta\) and with \(\eta_0=0\), while Condition 2F as stated fails because \(\Delta\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}^*\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}\) loses two derivatives; (b) \(\|\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}h\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}\ge c_\star\|h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\ge c_\star\|h\|_{H^{-1}(\Omega)}\), which is the estimate of Nickl’s Condition 2E (the stability estimate \(\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\theta_0)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}\ge c\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{H^{-1}}\) for the solution map \(\mathscr{G}\)) with the linearization \(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}\) in place of \(\mathscr{G}\) and the stronger norm \(L^2\) rather than \(H^{-1}\); (c) the Gaussian measure \(\mathcal{N}_{\theta_0}=N\big(0,T(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}^*\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\big)=N\big(0,T\operatorname{diag}\Theta_p(T)^{-1}\big)\) has per block covariance \(T\Theta_p(T)^{-1}\) with \(\|T\Theta_p(T)^{-1}\|\le T/\lambda_{\min}(\Theta_p(T))\le4(\lambda_1+\kappa a^2)/\lambda_1\) uniformly in \(p\) and in \(T\), so that \(\mathcal{N}_{\theta_0}\) is tight on \(H^{-s}(\mathbb{T}^d)\) for every \(s>d/2\).

Proposition 17.8, page 364 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\kappa\ne0\) be real, \(d\in\{1,2\}\), \(\Omega=\mathbb{T}^d\) and \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\), and let \(u,v\) solve \(i\partial_tu+\Delta u=\kappa|u|^2u\) on \([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\) with initial data \(\theta,\vartheta\) in \(H^1\) if \(d=1\) and in \(H^2\) if \(d=2\); write \(\mathscr{G}(\theta)=u_\theta\) for the solution map. Suppose \(\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le M_\infty\) and \(\|v(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le M_\infty\) for \(t\le T\), with \(M_\infty>0\). Then for \(t\le T\), \(e^{-6|\kappa|M_\infty^2t}\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\le\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\le e^{6|\kappa|M_\infty^2t}\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\), and, with the unnormalized norm of \(L^2(\mathcal{X})\), \(\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\vartheta)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2\ge\dfrac{1-e^{-6|\kappa|M_\infty^2T}}{6|\kappa|M_\infty^2}\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\ge Te^{-6|\kappa|M_\infty^2T}\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{H^{-1}(\Omega)}^2\). A bound \(M_\infty=M_\infty(T,\kappa,B)\) valid for all data in a ball of radius \(B\) exists in each of the following cases: (a) \(d=1\), either sign of \(\kappa\), every ball of \(H^1\); (b) \(d=2\), \(\kappa>0\), every ball of \(H^2\) (by Theorem 1.1 of Planchon, Tzvetkov and Visciglia (2017), applied to the \(H^2\) norm); (c) \(d=2\), \(\kappa<0\), the balls of \(H^2\) with \(2|\kappa|C_2B^2T<1\), where \(C_2\) is a constant such that \(\||f|^2f\|_{H^2}\le C_2\|f\|_{H^2}^3\). On such a ball Nickl’s Condition 2E holds for \(\mathscr{G}\) (the stability estimate \(\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\vartheta)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}\ge c\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{H^{-1}}\)), with the stronger norm \(L^2\) on the right and the constant \(c=T^{1/2}e^{-3|\kappa|M_\infty^2T}\); Condition 2A (uniform \(L^\infty\) bounds) holds with the bound \(M_\infty\); and the upper bound gives the \(L^2\) Lipschitz estimate of Condition 2B, \(\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\vartheta)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2\le\dfrac{e^{6|\kappa|M_\infty^2T}-1}{6|\kappa|M_\infty^2}\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\).

Proposition 17.10, page 366 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider the linear Schrödinger equation \(i\partial_tu=-\Delta u\) on \(\mathbb{T}^d\), \(u_\theta(t)=e^{it\Delta}\theta=\sum_je^{-i\lambda_jt}\theta_je_j\) for \(\theta\in L^2(\mathbb{T}^d;\mathbb{C})\), where \(e_j(x)=e^{2\pi ik_j\cdot x}\) is the Fourier basis and \(\lambda_j=4\pi^2|k_j|^2\asymp j^{2/d}\) is nondecreasing. The data \(Z^{(N)}\) are \(Y_i=u_{\theta_0}(t_i,x_i)+\varepsilon_i\) at \(N\) independent points \((t_i,x_i)\) uniform on \([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\), with noise whose real and imaginary parts are independent standard Gaussian, where \(\theta_0\) is the true initial condition. The prior is the Gaussian series prior of Nickl, \(\theta=\sum_{j\le D}\theta_je_j\) truncated to the first \(D=D_N\) modes, in which the real and the imaginary part of \(\theta_j\) are independent with precision \(\rho^{-2}\lambda_j^\alpha\), where \(\rho^{-2}=N\delta_N^2\), \(\delta_N=N^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), \(\alpha=\gamma\) and \(\gamma>d/2\). Let \(\tilde\theta_N\) be the posterior mean, let \(\Phi_{ij}=e^{-i\lambda_jt_i}e_j(x_i)\) be the design matrix with adjoint summary \((\Phi^*Y)_j=\sum_ie^{i\lambda_jt_i}\overline{e_j(x_i)}Y_i\), and let \(N(0,\operatorname{Id})\) denote complex white noise, whose real and imaginary parts are independent with covariance \(\operatorname{Id}\). Then: (a) the posterior is exactly Gaussian, the adjoint summary \(\Phi^*Y\) together with the design is exactly sufficient, and the quantile map of generative Bayesian computation (the map from the summary to the posterior quantiles) is exactly affine, with per mode scale \((N+\rho^{-2}\lambda_j^\alpha)^{-1/2}\) in the real and in the imaginary part when the Gram matrix \(\Phi^*\Phi\) of the design is replaced by its limit \(N\operatorname{Id}\); (b) if \(D_N\to\infty\) and \(D_N=o(N^{d/(2\gamma+d)})\), then \(\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-a}}\big(\operatorname{Law}(\sqrt N(\theta-\tilde\theta_N)\mid Z^{(N)}),N(0,\operatorname{Id})\big)\to0\) in probability (under the data law with true initial condition \(\theta_0\)) for every \(a>d/2\), where \(\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-a}}\) is the Wasserstein distance of order one on \(H^{-a}(\mathbb{T}^d;\mathbb{C})\); (c) if in addition \(\theta_0\in H^\gamma\) and \(N\lambda_{D_N}^{-(a+\gamma)}\to0\), then \(\sqrt N(\tilde\theta_N-\theta_0)\xrightarrow{d}N(0,\operatorname{Id})\) in \(H^{-a}\); the choice \(D_N\asymp N^{d/(2\gamma+d)}/\log N\) meets the conditions of (b) and (c) for every \(a>d/2\); (d) (b) and (c) hold with \(u_\theta(t)\), \(u_{\tilde\theta_N}(t)\) and \(u_{\theta_0}(t)\) in place of \(\theta\), \(\tilde\theta_N\) and \(\theta_0\), at every \(t\) and uniformly in \(t\), with the same limit \(e^{it\Delta}_\#N(0,\operatorname{Id})=N(0,\operatorname{Id})\), and no supremum norm statement holds at any \(t\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m4d.tex, label m:prop:sch.




Corollary 17.11, page 370 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Work in the setting of the linear Schrödinger transfer result: data from the linear Schrödinger equation \(i\partial_tu=-\Delta u\) on \(\mathbb{T}^d\) with true initial condition \(\theta_0\in H^\gamma\), \(\gamma>d/2\), observed with noise whose real and imaginary parts are independent standard Gaussian at \(N\) independent uniform points of \([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\); the Gaussian series prior of Nickl truncated to the first \(D_N\) modes, with precision \(\rho^{-2}\lambda_j^\gamma\) for the real and for the imaginary part of the \(j\)th coefficient, \(\rho^{-2}=N\delta_N^2\), \(\delta_N=N^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\); the exact posterior \(\Pi_N\) with mean \(\tilde\theta_N\); \(D_N\to\infty\), \(D_N=o(N^{d/(2\gamma+d)})\); and, for a fixed \(a>d/2\), \(N\lambda_{D_N}^{-(a+\gamma)}\to0\). Let \(\widehat\Pi_N\) be a measure produced by generative Bayesian computation (GBC), with mean \(\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N\), such that \(\sqrt N\,\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-a}}(\widehat\Pi_N,\Pi_N)\to0\) in probability (the exact posterior \(\widehat\Pi_N=\Pi_N\) satisfies this). Let \(N(0,\operatorname{Id})\) denote complex white noise, whose real and imaginary parts are independent with covariance \(\operatorname{Id}\). Then: (i) \(\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-a}}\big(\operatorname{Law}(\sqrt N(\theta-\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N)\mid\theta\sim\widehat\Pi_N),N(0,\operatorname{Id})\big)\to0\) in probability and \(\sqrt N(\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N-\theta_0)\xrightarrow{d}N(0,\operatorname{Id})\) in \(H^{-a}\); (ii) the statements of (i) hold for \(u_\theta(t)\), \(u_{\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N}(t)\) and \(u_{\theta_0}(t)\) at every \(t\), uniformly in \(t\), with the same limit; (iii) for a map \(\Phi:H^{-a}\to\mathbb{B}\) into a Banach space \(\mathbb{B}\) that is Hadamard differentiable at \(u_{\theta_0}(t)\), \(\sqrt N\big(\Phi(u_{\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N}(t))-\Phi(u_{\theta_0}(t))\big)\xrightarrow{d}\dot\Phi_{u_{\theta_0}(t)}[W]\) with \(W\sim N(0,\operatorname{Id})\), and the ball in \(H^{-a}\) about \(\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N\) of \(\widehat\Pi_N\) probability \(1-\beta\) contains \(\theta_0\) with probability tending to \(1-\beta\) under the data law with true initial condition \(\theta_0\); (iv) under the data law with true initial condition \(\theta_0+h/\sqrt N\), for every \(h\in H^\gamma\), (i) to (iii) hold with \(\theta_0+h/\sqrt N\) in place of \(\theta_0\), so that \(\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N\) is a regular estimator sequence, and for \(\psi\in H^a\) the limit \(N(0,\|\psi\|_{L^2}^2)\) of \(\sqrt N\,\mathrm{Re}\langle\psi,\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N-\theta_0\rangle\) is the efficient one, so that \(\mathrm{Re}\langle\psi,\hat\theta^{\mathrm G}_N\rangle\) is efficient among regular estimator sequences of \(\mathrm{Re}\langle\psi,\theta\rangle\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/m4d.tex, label m:cor:schtransfer.




Open Question 17.12, page 371 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open question. For the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \(i\partial_tu+\Delta u=\kappa|u|^2u\) on \(\mathbb{T}^d\) (\(d\le2\)), one computes the information operator \(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}^*\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}\) of the linearization (adjoint in unnormalized \(L^2([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d)\)) about a constant background \(\theta_0=a\) exactly, mode by mode, through the Bogoliubov dispersion relation. Extend this to a multimode background \(u_0\): write \(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}^*\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}=T\operatorname{Id}+\mathcal{R}+\mathcal{K}\) with \(\mathcal{K}\) compact and \(\mathcal{R}\) supported on the four wave resonant manifold \(\{(k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4):k_1+k_2=k_3+k_4,\ \lambda_{k_1}+\lambda_{k_2}=\lambda_{k_3}+\lambda_{k_4}\}\), where \(\lambda_k=4\pi^2|k|^2\), and characterize the triples \((\kappa,\theta_0,T)\) for which \(T\operatorname{Id}+\mathcal{R}\) is uniformly invertible. In the focusing case, prove a Bernstein von Mises theorem for fixed \(T\) with constants exponential in the largest modulational growth rate.

Proposition 17.13, page 372 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((X_t)\) be a Markov process, \(V_{t+1}\) a payoff with \(\mathbb{E}V_{t+1}^2<\infty\), \(C_t(x)=\mathbb{E}[V_{t+1}\mid X_t=x]\) the continuation value, and \(L_1,\dots,L_K\) basis functions such that the \(L_k(X_t)\) are square integrable and linearly independent in \(L^2\). As the number of simulated paths grows, the Longstaff Schwartz regression coefficients \(\hat\beta_t=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_\beta\sum_m\big(V^{(m)}_{t+1}-\sum_k\beta_kL_k(X^{(m)}_t)\big)^2\) converge almost surely to the coefficients of the \(L^2\) projection of \(C_t\) onto \(\mathrm{span}\{L_k\}\) (the strong law for least squares), and \(C_t(x)\) is the posterior mean summary \(\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S]\) for the “parameter” \(\theta=V_{t+1}\) given the “data” \(S=X_t\). Conversely, Step 2 of the generative Bayesian computation (GBC) algorithm (the fit of a generator of the parameter given the summary on the training pairs simulated in Step 1, with \(\theta^{(m)}\) drawn from the prior and \(Z^{(m)}\) from the model) with the mean regression loss and basis functions of the summary \(S_N\) is an LSM regression with the following roles: paths correspond to prior draws \(\theta^{(m)}\), the state \(X_t\) to the summary \(S_N(Z^{(m)})\), the payoff \(V_{t+1}\) to \(\theta^{(m)}\), and the continuation value to the posterior mean \(\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S_N]\). In the linear Gaussian case (the linear model \(Y=\Phi\theta+\varepsilon\) with standard Gaussian noise, a Gaussian prior and \(S_N=\Phi^\top Y\) the adjoint statistic), with the design held fixed, the posterior mean is linear in \(S_N\), so a linear basis is exact, just as LSM with a linear basis is exact when the continuation value is linear in the state.
Source: source/chapters/ext/m4e.tex, label m:prop:lsm.




Theorem 17.14, page 373 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption (Assumption U), in case (c) only.
Statement. Let \(\Pi\) be a prior on \(\theta\), taking values in \(\mathbb{R}^D\) or in a separable Hilbert space, with \(\mathbb{E}\|\theta\|^2<\infty\); let data \(Z\) be drawn from the observation model given \(\theta\) and let \(S=S_N(Z)\) be a summary statistic. Let \((\theta^{(m)},S^{(m)})_{m\le M}\) be independent draws of \((\theta,S)\) from this prior predictive law (Step 1 of generative Bayesian computation), let \(\operatorname{Law}(S)\) be the law of \(S\), let \(\{L_k\}\) be an orthonormal basis of \(L^2(\operatorname{Law}(S))\), and let \(\hat m_{K,M}(s)=\sum_{k\le K}\hat\beta_kL_k(s)\) be the least squares regression of \(\theta^{(m)}\) on \(L_1(S^{(m)}),\dots,L_K(S^{(m)})\), coordinate by coordinate. Then for fixed \(K\), \(\hat m_{K,M}\to m_K:=\sum_{k\le K}\langle\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S],L_k\rangle L_k\) almost surely in \(L^2(\operatorname{Law}(S))\) as \(M\to\infty\), and \(m_K\to\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S]\) in \(L^2(\operatorname{Law}(S))\) as \(K\to\infty\). If moreover \(\sum_{k\le K}L_k(s)^2\le bK\) for all \(s\) and \(K\) and some constant \(b\) (as for a basis bounded by \(\sqrt b\)), and \(K_M\to\infty\) with \(K_M\log K_M/M\to0\), then \(\hat m_{K_M,M}\to\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S]\) in \(L^2(\operatorname{Law}(S))\) in probability. The regression recovers \(\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S]\), the posterior mean given the summary, and not the posterior mean \(m(Z)=\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid Z^{(N)}]\) itself: always \(\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S]=\mathbb{E}[m(Z)\mid S]\), and this equals \(m(Z)\) if and only if \(m(Z)\) is \(\sigma(S)\) measurable. Moreover: (a) if \(S=m(Z)\) then \(\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S]=S=m(Z)\) exactly, for every \(N\); (b) if, in the linear model \(Y=\Phi\theta+\varepsilon\) with standard Gaussian noise and Gaussian prior, \(S\) is the adjoint statistic \(\Phi^\top Y\) with the design held at its observed value in Step 1, or the pair \((\Phi^\top Y,\Phi^\top\Phi)\) when the design is drawn afresh, then \(S\) is sufficient and \(\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S]=m(Z)\) exactly, for every \(N\); (c) if \(S=\hat S^{J_N}_N\) is the one step efficient score statistic (a cross fitted Gauss Newton step from a preliminary estimate, projected on the first \(J_N\) modes), then, under Assumption U for \(S_N=\hat S^{J_N}_N\) (a uniform Bernstein von Mises statement) and the hypotheses of the proposition equating this statistic with Nickl’s efficient centering (among them Conditions 1 and 2 of Nickl (2024) and the rate and Lipschitz weight conditions of that proposition), \(\sqrt N\,\|\mathbb{E}[\theta\mid S]-m(Z)\|_{H^{-k-2}}\to0\) in probability, where \(k\) is the Sobolev index of Nickl’s Bernstein von Mises theorem. Consequently, under (a) or (b) the regression summary \(\hat m_{K_M,M}(S)\), the center of the GBC posterior built on it, converges to the exact posterior mean \(m(Z)\) in the double limit, in \(L^2(\operatorname{Law}(S))\), that is, on average over the prior predictive law of the data and not at a fixed observed value; under (c) it agrees with it only to \(o(N^{-1/2})\) in \(H^{-k-2}\).

Proposition 17.15, page 376 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider the linear model \(Y=\Phi\theta+\varepsilon\) with unit variance Gaussian noise and Gaussian prior \(\theta\sim N(0,\Sigma_0)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^D\), in which the \(i\)th row of the design matrix \(\Phi\) is \(\phi_i^\top\) with \(\phi_i=(s_j(t_i)e_j(x_i))_{j\le D}\) (\(s_j(t)\) being the time factor of the diagonal linear evolution, for example \(e^{-\nu\lambda_jt}\) for the heat equation), and order the observations by time. The sufficient statistic \(S_n=\Phi_{1:n}^\top Y_{1:n}\) and the Gram matrix \(G_n=\Phi_{1:n}^\top\Phi_{1:n}\) of the first \(n\) observations satisfy the recursions \(S_{n+1}=S_n+\phi_{n+1}Y_{n+1}\) and \(G_{n+1}=G_n+\phi_{n+1}\phi_{n+1}^\top\), and the posterior after \(n\) observations is \(N\big((G_n+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}S_n,\,(G_n+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\big)\). Consequently the sequential scheme that carries \((S_n,G_n)\) and, at each step, draws particles independently from this Gaussian is exact: \((S_n,G_n)\) is a deterministic function of the first \(n\) observations, each new observation is absorbed by the rank one update above, and every particle is an exact draw from the posterior after \(n\) observations.

Open Question 17.17, page 380 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open question. Let \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) be the torus (written \(\mathbb{T}^d\) when it is the domain of a network), \(T>0\) and \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\). The data are \(Z^{(N)}=(Y_i,X_i)_{i\le N}\) with \(Y_i=u_\theta(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\), where \(u_\theta=\mathscr{G}(\theta)\) is the solution of an evolution equation with initial condition \(\theta\) (in the setting of Nickl (2024), \(\partial_tu=\Delta u+F(u)\), \(u(0)=\theta\)), the \(X_i\) are i.i.d. uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\) and the \(\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,I_W)\) are independent of them. Let \(\theta_0\) be the true initial condition, \(P^N_{\theta_0}\) the law of the data, \(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}\) the linearization of \(\mathscr{G}\) at \(\theta_0\), with adjoint \(\mathbb{I}^*_{\theta_0}\) taken with respect to \(L^2(\Omega)\) and the unnormalized \(L^2(\mathcal{X})\), and \(\mathcal{N}_{\theta_0}=N\big(0,T(\mathbb{I}^*_{\theta_0}\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\big)\).
Nickl’s Bernstein von Mises theorem (Theorem 2 of Nickl (2024)) is for the Gaussian series prior \(\Pi\), the law of \((\sqrt N\delta_N)^{-1}\sum_j\lambda_j^{-\gamma/2}g_je_j\), where \((e_j)\) is the Laplace eigenbasis of \(\Omega\) with eigenvalues \(\lambda_j\asymp j^{2/d}\), the \(g_j\) are i.i.d. \(N(0,1)\) and \(\delta_N=N^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) (its reproducing kernel Hilbert space is \(H_0^\gamma\)). It assumes, for the forward map on Sobolev balls, (A) uniform \(L^\infty\) bounds, (B) \(L^2\) Lipschitz continuity, (C) a linearization \(\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}\) with quadratic remainder, (D) \(L^\infty\) mapping properties from \(H^\zeta\) with \(\zeta>d/2\), (E) the stability estimate \(\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\theta_0)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}\ge c\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{H^{-1}}\) and (F) invertibility of the information operator (\(\Delta\mathbb{I}^*_{\theta_0}\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0}\) a homeomorphism of \(H^\eta_0\) for \(\eta\ge\eta_0\)), with integer \(\gamma>\max(3\zeta+3d/2+2,\eta_0)\) and \(k>\max(\zeta+5d/2,\eta_0)\). Its conclusion is that, with \(\tilde\theta_N=\mathbb{E}^\Pi[\theta\mid Z^{(N)}]\) the posterior mean, \(\mathscr{W}_1\big(\operatorname{Law}(\sqrt N(\theta-\tilde\theta_N)\mid Z^{(N)}),\mathcal{N}_{\theta_0}\big)\to0\) in \(P^N_{\theta_0}\) probability, where \(\mathscr{W}_1\) is the Wasserstein distance of order one on \(H^{-k-2}(\Omega)\), and \(\sqrt N(\tilde\theta_N-\theta_0)\to\mathcal{N}_{\theta_0}\) in distribution in \(H^{-k-2}\).
The Polson Ročková prior (Polson and Ročková (2018)) is the spike and slab prior on the weights of deep ReLU networks \(\theta:\mathbb{T}^d\to\mathbb{R}\), with hyperpriors on the width and the sparsity and a depth of order \(\log N\). The book’s theorem on posterior contraction under this prior (catalog entry contraction_under_a_network_prior) states that if the forward map satisfies Conditions 2A, 2B and 2E on \(L^\infty\) balls and \(\theta_0\in C^\alpha(\mathbb{T}^d)\) with \(d/2+1<\alpha<p\), where \(p\) is the input dimension of the networks, then with \(\epsilon_N=N^{-\alpha/(2\alpha+p)}\log^\delta N\), \(\delta>1\), the posterior contracts around \(\theta_0\) at the rate \(\epsilon_N\) for \(\mathscr{G}(\theta)\) in \(L^2(\mathcal{X})\) and for \(\theta\) in \(H^{-1}\), without knowledge of \(\alpha\). This gives rates and not the Gaussian limit, coverage or efficiency.
Nickl’s proof perturbs the parameter along the direction \(p_N(\bar\psi_{\theta_0})/\sqrt N\), where \(\psi\) is a test function, \(\bar\psi_{\theta_0}=T(\mathbb{I}^*_{\theta_0}\mathbb{I}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\psi\) and \(p_N\) is the projection onto the first \(J_N\asymp N\delta_N^2\) Laplace modes, and compares the prior with its shift by the Cameron Martin theorem. A network prior has no Cameron Martin theorem, and the shifted network \(\theta-t\,p_N(\bar\psi_{\theta_0})/\sqrt N\) is not a network of the same architecture. Wang and Ročková (2020) circumvent this in the direct model (nonparametric regression \(Y=f(X)+\varepsilon\)), for a constant weight, by absorbing the shift exactly into the intercept of the top layer and by a change of measure bound for the spike and slab weights; for a smooth non constant weight, the case needed here, they assume a no bias condition on the projection of the weight onto the random network features, so that the approximation step for \(\bar\psi_{\theta_0}\) is itself open there.
Extend Wang and Ročková (2020) to the inverse problem: prove the conclusion of Theorem 2 of Nickl (2024) as stated above with the Gaussian series prior replaced by the Polson Ročková prior, uniformly over the test functions \(\psi\) of the functional limit in a Sobolev ball, by absorbing the perturbation direction \(p_N(\bar\psi_{\theta_0})/\sqrt N\) into the last layer. Here the functional limit is the Gaussian limit of the posterior of the linear functional \(\langle\psi,\theta\rangle\), and the Sobolev ball is written \(U(\kappa+2,1)\) in the book: the ball of radius one in the mean zero Sobolev space \(H_0^{\kappa+2}\) (the notation \(U(r,B)\) is that of Nickl (2024)), with \(\kappa\) the Sobolev index of Nickl’s proof, \(2d+\zeta<\kappa<k-d/2\). For the inverse problem \(\bar\psi_{\theta_0}\) is smooth whenever \(\psi\) is, by the mapping properties in Theorem 2.6 of Konen and Nickl (2026), which is the smoothness that the approximation step needs; what remains is the change of measure step and the uniformity in \(\psi\in U(\kappa+2,1)\) needed for the functional theorem.
With the contraction theorem above, this would give generative Bayesian computation (GBC) under this adaptive prior all the conclusions of the book’s transfer theorem for GBC (catalog entry bvm_for_gbc).

Open Question 17.18, page 380 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open question. Prove the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption (Assumption U of the book), with the rate \(\bar\epsilon_N\to0\) used in the book’s theorem on the identity skip quantile generator. Assumption U: for a summary statistic \(S_N\), a prior \(\Pi\), a true parameter \(\theta_0\), observations on \([0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^d\), the linearization \(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\) at \(\vartheta\) of the solution map, \(\mathcal{N}_\vartheta=N\big(0,T(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta^*\mathbb{I}_\vartheta)^{-1}\big)\), and Sobolev indices \(k\) and \(\zeta>d/2\) as in Nickl’s Bernstein von Mises theorem and Condition 2D, there is a set \(\Theta_N\) of parameters such that (U1) \(\Pi(\Theta_N)\to1\), \(\theta_0\in\Theta_N\) for all large \(N\), and \(\bar\epsilon_N:=\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta_N}\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{N}}_\vartheta\,\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-k-2}}\big(\operatorname{Law}(\sqrt N(\theta-S_N)\mid Z^{(N)}),\mathcal{N}_\vartheta\big)\to0\), where \(\mathbb{E}^{\mathbb{N}}_\vartheta\) is the expectation under the data law with parameter \(\vartheta\); (U2) these discrepancies are uniformly integrable under the prior predictive law; (U3) \(\vartheta\mapsto T(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta^*\mathbb{I}_\vartheta)^{-1}\) is Lipschitz from \((\Theta_N,\|\cdot\|_{H^\zeta})\) into bounded operators \(H^{-k-2}\to H^{-k-4}\) and \(\vartheta\mapsto\mathcal{N}_\vartheta\) is Lipschitz from \((\Theta_N,\|\cdot\|_{H^\zeta})\) into the probability measures on \(H^{-k-2}\) with the distance \(\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-k-2}}\), both with constants that do not depend on \(N\), the first moments \(\mathrm{m}_1(\vartheta)=\int\|x\|_{H^{-k-2}}\,\mathrm{d}\mathcal{N}_\vartheta(x)\) satisfy \(\int_{\Theta_N^c}\mathrm{m}_1\,\mathrm{d}\Pi\to0\) and \(\Pi(\Theta_N^c)\sup_{\Theta_N}\mathrm{m}_1\to0\), \(S_N\in\Theta_N\) with probability tending to one, and \(\mathbb{E}^\Pi[\|\theta-S_N\|_{H^\zeta}\mid S_N]\to0\); (U4) for every \(\theta_0\in\Theta_N\), \(\mathbb{E}\big[\mathscr{W}_{1,H^{-k-2}}\big(\operatorname{Law}(\sqrt N(\theta-S_N)\mid Z^{(N)}),\mathcal{N}_{\theta_0}\big)\,\big|\,S_N\big]\to0\) in probability under the data law with true parameter \(\theta_0\). The proof is to proceed by tracking the constants of Theorem 2 of Nickl (2024) and Theorem 2.8 of Konen and Nickl (2026) over the localization sets, and the same is asked for the uniform second moment bound used in the book’s proposition on the one step summary under four approximate Bayesian computation criteria.

Open Question 17.19, page 380 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open question. Consider the localized generative Bayesian computation (GBC) of the book for the initial condition \(\theta\) of a time evolution equation, observed at \(N\) independent uniform space time points \(X_i\) as \(Y_i=u_\theta(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\), with \(u_\theta=\mathscr{G}(\theta)\) and noise \(\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,I_W)\), with a Gaussian prior of covariance \(\Sigma_0\) on \(D\) retained Laplace modes. Let \(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta\) be the linearization (Jacobian) of \(\mathscr{G}\) at \(\vartheta\) and \(\mathbb{I}_\vartheta^*\) its adjoint. A preliminary estimate \(\bar\theta_N\) is computed from the data. With the residuals \(r_i=Y_i-u_{\bar\theta_N}(X_i)\), the realized information \(F_N=\mathbb{I}^*_{\bar\theta_N}\mathbb{I}_{\bar\theta_N}\) of the \(N\) observations on the observed design and the Gauss Newton covariance \(\Sigma_N=(F_N+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\), the summary of the data is the regularized one step Gauss Newton summary \(S=\bar\theta_N+\Sigma_N\big(\mathbb{I}^*_{\bar\theta_N}\big[\sum_ir_i\delta_{X_i}\big]-\Sigma_0^{-1}\bar\theta_N\big)\), which linearizes the forward map once, at \(\bar\theta_N\). The training parameters \(\theta^{(m)}\), \(m\le M\), are drawn from the proposal \(q_c=N(\bar\theta_N,c^2\Sigma_N)\), where the localization radius \(c\) is measured in posterior standard deviations, the training data are simulated from them, and a head (the part of the generator that models the residuals \(\theta^{(m)}-S^{(m)}\) of the summary \(S^{(m)}\) of the \(m\)th training data) is fitted from the \(M\) pairs.
The book’s decomposition of the error of the localized generator reads, under Conditions 2A to 2D of Nickl (2024) and the hypotheses of the book’s theorem on the residual law under a localized proposal (a linear Gaussian model whose prior covariance and Gram matrix are diagonalized by one orthonormal basis), and with the residuals centered so that their mean is removed, \(\mathcal{E}(c)^2\asymp\beta(c)^2+a_v/c^{v}+b\,c^4\). Here \(\mathcal{E}(c)\) is the Wasserstein error of the localized generator, in posterior standard deviations; \(v=0\) for the identity head (the head that adds to the summary a Gaussian whose covariance is fitted to the training residuals) and \(v=2\) for an affine head (an affine function of the summary fitted by regression, whose slope is estimated from a design of spread \(c\)); \(a_v\asymp D/M\); \(b\asymp c_3^2/N\), with \(c_3\) the third derivative constant of the log likelihood in the Hessian metric; and \(\beta(c)=\frac1D\sum_{j\le D}\big|\sqrt{s_j+c^2p_j^2}-1\big|\), where \(p_1,\dots,p_D\) are the eigenvalues of the prior fraction operator \(P=\Sigma_N\Sigma_0^{-1}\) (so \(p_j\) is the fraction of the posterior precision in direction \(j\) supplied by the prior) and \(s_j=1-p_j\). The first term is the exact population bias of localization, the second is the Monte Carlo variance of the head, and the third is the leading term of a Taylor expansion of the relinearization error, so the decomposition is an expansion and not a two sided bound: the symbol \(\asymp\) matches orders term by term, with constants that are not tracked.
In the linear model \(Y=\Phi\theta+\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,\varsigma^2\operatorname{Id})\), with prior \(N(0,\Sigma_0)\), \(F=\Phi^\top\Phi/\varsigma^2\) and \(\Sigma_N=(F+\Sigma_0^{-1})^{-1}\), the summary \(S(Y)=\bar\theta+\Sigma_N\big(\Phi^\top(Y-\Phi\bar\theta)/\varsigma^2-\Sigma_0^{-1}\bar\theta\big)\) equals \(\Sigma_N(F\theta+\Phi^\top\varepsilon/\varsigma^2)\) for every point \(\bar\theta\): it is the posterior mean and does not depend on the linearization point. The term \(b\,c^4\) is therefore purely a nonlinear effect, and it arises because the summary is linearized once, at \(\bar\theta_N\). Iterating the Gauss Newton step means repeating the step above from each new iterate in place of \(\bar\theta_N\), with the Jacobian recomputed at the iterate from the data alone, at a cost of \(D+1\) forward solves per training draw for each extra step; recomputing it at the training parameter \(\theta^{(m)}\) would not define a statistic, since that parameter is not available for the observed data. The claim to be confirmed is that the decomposition then reduces to \(\beta(c)^2+a_v/c^{v}\), which for the affine head decreases in \(c\) until the bias \(\beta(c)\) begins to grow, so that the optimal radius moves out to where the localization bias binds, and the achievable error is within \(O(\sqrt{D/M})\) of the smallest value of \(\beta(c)\), the floor it approaches as \(M\) grows. A numerical confirmation exists: in the numerical study of Polson and Sokolov (2026), with a two step Gauss Newton summary for the six mode (\(D=6\)) two dimensional Navier Stokes problem of the book’s experiments, the \(c^4\) term disappeared, and the error of the affine head (Wasserstein distance to a Metropolis reference chain, in posterior standard deviations) at \(c=6\) fell from \(0.37\) to \(0.16\) and became flat in \(c\).
Confirm this: for the summary obtained by iterating the Gauss Newton step, with the Jacobian recomputed from the data alone at each iterate, show that the \(c^4\) term disappears from the decomposition for the converged iterate, find how fast it decays with the number of steps, and determine whether, in a nonlinear problem, the resulting error falls below the error of the Laplace approximation, an error of order \(c_3\sqrt{J^3/N}\) in the classical bounds, with \(c_3\) a bound on the third derivatives of the log likelihood and \(J\) the dimension of the parameter. Here the Laplace approximation is the Gaussian approximation of the posterior at the maximum a posteriori estimate, with covariance the inverse of the negative Hessian of the log posterior density there.

Open Question 17.20, page 381 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open question. Let \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) be the torus, \(T>0\) and \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\). The data are \(Z^{(N)}=(Y_i,X_i)_{i\le N}\) with \(Y_i=u_\theta(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\), where \(u_\theta=\mathscr{G}(\theta)\) solves an evolution equation with initial condition \(\theta\), the \(X_i\) are i.i.d. uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\) and the \(\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,I_W)\) are independent of them. Let \(\Pi_N\) be the exact posterior of \(\theta\), \((e_j)\) the Laplace eigenbasis of \(\Omega\) and \(S_N\) a summary statistic of the data. Generative Bayesian computation (GBC) simulates \(M\) training pairs, a parameter drawn from the prior and the summary of data drawn from the model given that parameter, trains a conditional generator \(\widehat G(s,U)\), with \(U\) a base random variable independent of everything, so that \(\operatorname{Law}(\widehat G(s,U))\) approximates \(\operatorname{Law}(\theta\mid S_N(Z)=s)\), in coefficient form \(\widehat G(s,U)=\sum_j\widehat Q_j(U_j\mid s)e_j\) with \(\widehat Q_j(\cdot\mid s)\) a learned conditional quantile function. The GBC posterior is \(\widehat\Pi_N=\operatorname{Law}\big(\widehat G(S_N(Z^{(N)}),U)\big)\) given the observed data \(Z^{(N)}\). The true conditional quantile map is \((\tau,s)\mapsto Q_j(\tau\mid s)\), the \(\tau\) quantile of the \(j\)th coefficient \(\langle\theta,e_j\rangle\) of \(\theta\) given \(S_N(Z)=s\).
The book’s transfer theorem for GBC (catalog entry bvm_for_gbc) is a \(\sqrt N\) statement: if \(\sqrt N\,\mathscr{W}_1(\widehat\Pi_N,\Pi_N)\to0\) in probability, where \(\mathscr{W}_1\) is the Wasserstein distance of order one on the negative Sobolev space \(H^{-k-2}(\Omega)\) of Nickl’s Bernstein von Mises theorem, and \(\widehat\Pi_N\) concentrates on the localization set of Nickl’s proof with bounded moments, then \(\widehat\Pi_N\) has the same Gaussian limit as the exact posterior \(\Pi_N\), together with the further conclusions about the trajectory, coverage and efficiency listed in that entry.
The book has two finite \(N\) checks, and neither is a quantification. The first is linear: the heat equation \(\partial_tu=\nu\Delta u\), \(u(0)=\theta\) on \(\Omega=[0,1]\) with \(\nu=0.01\) and \(T=1\), a fixed Gaussian prior on the initial condition (not rescaled with \(N\)), with independent coefficients on the twenty modes \(|k|\le20\) of variances \(\sigma_{0,k}^2=\rho^2\lambda_k^{-\alpha}\), \(\alpha=3\), \(\lambda_k=4\pi^2k^2\), and the exact conjugate Gaussian posterior. With the scale \(\rho\) calibrated so that the prior standard deviation at \(|k|=1\) matches the true initial condition (\(\rho=124.0\)), the largest relative discrepancy over twenty modes between the exact posterior standard deviation and the Bernstein von Mises scale with the prior precision added, \((N\iota_k+\sigma_{0,k}^{-2})^{-1/2}\), where \(\iota_k=(1-e^{-2\nu\lambda_kT})/(2\nu\lambda_kT)\) is the information per mode, is \(6.05\times10^{-3}\) at \(N=2000\), \(1.60\times10^{-3}\) at \(N=5\times10^4\) and \(7.77\times10^{-4}\) at \(N=1.3\times10^6\). The second is nonlinear: two dimensional Navier Stokes on the \(2\pi\) periodic torus with \(\nu=5\times10^{-3}\) and \(T=1\), the initial vorticity in \(D=6\) real cosine modes with an independent Gaussian prior, the truth a draw from the prior, and \(N=80\) space time points observed with noise standard deviation \(0.45\). GBC and the Laplace approximation (the Gaussian approximation of the posterior at the maximum a posteriori estimate) are scored by their Wasserstein distance to a Metropolis reference chain, in units of posterior standard deviation, and two further regimes with \(N=25\) points (a larger amplitude, and a wider posterior) were run to look for the crossover at which non Gaussianity of the posterior would favor a simulation based method over the Laplace approximation. The crossover was not found, and neither regime made the posterior measurably less Gaussian than the main run.
Quantify the non Gaussian correction for the Taylor Green problem as a function of \(A/\nu\) and \(N\), and bound \(\mathscr{W}_1(\widehat\Pi_N,\Pi_N)\) nonasymptotically in terms of the generator approximation error for the true conditional quantile map. Here the Taylor Green problem is the inverse problem for the two dimensional Navier Stokes equations \(\partial_tu+\nu Au+B[u,u]=f\), \(u(0)=\theta\), on the \(2\pi\) periodic torus, with viscosity \(\nu\), Stokes operator \(A=-\Delta\) on divergence free mean zero fields, \(B[u,v]=P[(u\cdot\nabla)v]\) (\(P\) the projection onto divergence free fields) and \(f=0\), with true initial condition \(\theta_0=u_{\rm TG}(0)\), where \(u_{\rm TG}(t,x)=A\,e^{-2\nu t}(\sin x_1\cos x_2,\,-\cos x_1\sin x_2)\) is the Taylor Green vortex of amplitude \(A\), an exact solution for \(f=0\). The book measures the ratio of the advective coupling to the viscous decay at wavenumber \(k\) in the equation linearized about this vortex as \(cA/(\nu|k|)\) with \(c\approx0.91\).
The failure of the book’s experiments to find the crossover in any regime tested says that the answer cannot be assumed, and suggests the obstruction: the error of the Laplace approximation and the bias of GBC are governed by the same curvature of the forward map, measured in posterior standard deviations, so the two do not move independently.

Open Question 17.21, page 381 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open question. Let \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) be the torus, \(T>0\) and \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\), and let the data be \(Y_i=u_\theta(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\) at independent uniform space time points \(X_i\in\mathcal{X}\), with Gaussian noise \(\varepsilon_i\) and \(u_\theta=\mathscr{G}(\theta)\) the solution of an evolution equation with initial condition \(\theta\), the true initial condition being \(\theta_0\), as in the book’s transfer theorem for generative Bayesian computation (GBC) (catalog entry bvm_for_gbc): if the GBC posterior approximates the exact posterior with an error of smaller order than \(N^{-1/2}\) in Wasserstein distance and concentrates on the localization set of Nickl’s proof, it has the Gaussian limit of the exact posterior for the initial condition, together with the further conclusions about the trajectory, coverage and efficiency listed in that entry. This theorem and the Bernstein von Mises theorems of Nickl (2024) and of Konen and Nickl (2026) on which it rests assume deterministic dynamics without model error: every posterior draw is a solution of the equation and lies on the solution manifold \(\mathcal{M}=\{u_\theta\}\), and a trajectory generated with model error does not lie on \(\mathcal{M}\). In the state space formulation of Carlin, Polson and Stoffer (1992) the dynamics with model error are \(u_{k+1}=u_k+\Delta t\,F(u_k)+\sqrt{\Delta t}\,G\xi_k\), with time step \(\Delta t\), \(F\) the right hand side of the equation, innovations \(\xi_k\) and noise scale \(G\). The Gibbs smoother of Carlin, Polson and Stoffer is then the smoother for the initial condition problem: the forward edge \(p(u_{k+1}\mid u_k)\) is nonlinear in \(u_k\) through \(F\), the backward edge is Gaussian in \(u_k\), and a single move update samples \(u_k\) from their product. As \(G\to0\) the chain of transitions collapses to the deterministic solution map and the smoother degenerates to a sampler for \(\theta\) alone, which is the setting of Konen and Nickl (2026).
The Bayesian calibration framework of Kennedy and O’Hagan (2001), as made operational by Higdon and coauthors, runs the simulator at a design, fits a Gaussian process emulator of \(\theta\mapsto\mathscr{G}(\theta)\), adds a discrepancy process \(\delta\) and runs Markov chain Monte Carlo on \((\theta,\delta)\). The identifiability problem between \(\theta\) and \(\delta\) (Brynjarsdóttir and O’Hagan (2014); Tuo and Wu (2016)) is Condition 2E of Nickl (2024), the stability estimate \(\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\theta_0)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}\ge c\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{H^{-1}}\), in applied form: when the discrepancy can absorb a perturbation of \(\theta\), the information operator is not injective. The natural formulation is hierarchical, with \(\delta\) a Gaussian process of amplitude \(\sigma_N\to0\); for GBC it is trivial to include \(\delta\) in the simulation of the training pairs, and for the theory the admissible rate of \(\sigma_N\) is open.
Combine the transfer theorem with a discrepancy process of amplitude \(\sigma_N\) and identify the rate at which \(\sigma_N\) must tend to zero for the deterministic limit (the Gaussian limit of that theorem for dynamics without model error) to persist, connecting to the Gibbs smoother above and to the particle methods for state space models with static parameters (Storvik (2002); Carvalho, Johannes, Lopes and Polson (2010)). In the linear model without a latent state these particle systems collapse (the sufficient statistic is a deterministic function of the data, all weights are equal and there is nothing to resample), whereas with \(G\ne0\) the statistic depends on the sampled path, the weights are no longer equal, and the degeneracy of particles can occur.

Proposition 20.5, page 415 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. First stated in Carvalho, Johannes, Lopes and Polson (2010), Particle learning and smoothing, Statistical Science 25, 88 to 106.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider a state space model with a static parameter \(\theta\), hidden states \(x_t\) and observations \(y_t\), with the Markov structure of such a model: \(y_{t+1}\) depends on the past only through the essential state \(z_t=(x_t,s_t,\theta)\), and \(p(x_{t+1}\mid z_t,y_{1:t+1})=p(x_{t+1}\mid z_t,y_{t+1})\). Suppose there are conditional sufficient statistics \(s_t\), updated deterministically by \(s_{t+1}=S(s_t,x_t,x_{t+1},y_{t+1})\), such that \(p(\theta\mid x_{0:t},y_{1:t})=p(\theta\mid s_t)\). Particle learning updates the essential state in four steps: (1) resample \(z_t\) with weights proportional to the predictive likelihood \(p(y_{t+1}\mid z_t)=\int p(y_{t+1}\mid x_{t+1},\theta)\,p(x_{t+1}\mid x_t,\theta)\,\mathrm{d}x_{t+1}\); (2) propagate \(x_{t+1}\sim p(x_{t+1}\mid z_t,y_{t+1})\); (3) update \(s_{t+1}=S(s_t,x_t,x_{t+1},y_{t+1})\); (4) draw \(\theta\sim p(\theta\mid s_{t+1})\). Let \(z_t\) have the law \(p(z_t\mid y_{1:t})\). Reweight this law by the predictive likelihood \(p(y_{t+1}\mid z_t)\), which is step one at the level of laws, and then apply steps two to four. Then the new essential state \((x_{t+1},s_{t+1},\theta)\) has the law \(p(x_{t+1},s_{t+1},\theta\mid y_{1:t+1})\).

Theorem 20.9, page 423 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let the input spikes \(t_k\) form a Poisson process of rate \(\lambda>0\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). Attach to the \(k\)th spike a mark \((\tau_k,\kappa_k)\), the marks being independent with a common law \(M\) on \((0,\infty)^2\) and independent of the spike times, and given the marks let the amplitude \(A_k\) be exponential with rate \(\kappa_k\). Let \(V=\sum_{t_k\le t}A_k e^{-(t-t_k)/\tau_k}\) be the stationary potential at time \(t\). Then for every \(\theta>0\), with both sides possibly equal to \(+\infty\), \(-\log\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\theta V}=\lambda\int\tau\log\big(1+\theta/\kappa\big)\,M(\mathrm{d}\tau,\mathrm{d}\kappa)=\int\log\big(1+\theta/y\big)\,U(\mathrm{d}y)\), where \(U\) is the image of the measure \(\lambda\tau\,M(\mathrm{d}\tau,\mathrm{d}\kappa)\) under \((\tau,\kappa)\mapsto\kappa\). If \(\int\log(1+1/y)\,U(\mathrm{d}y)<\infty\), which is the condition that \(U\) be a Thorin measure, then \(V\) is a generalized Gamma convolution with Thorin measure \(U\) and zero drift, that is, \(\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\theta V}=\exp\big(-\int\log(1+\theta/y)\,U(\mathrm{d}y)\big)\) for \(\theta>0\). Otherwise \(V=\infty\) almost surely. In particular, if all marks equal \((\tau,\kappa)\) then \(V\) has the Gamma law with shape \(\lambda\tau\) and rate \(\kappa\), and if \(\tau_k\) and \(\kappa_k\) are independent and \(\kappa_k\) has law \(\nu\) then \(U=\lambda\,\mathbb{E}[\tau_k]\,\nu\).
