Open Question 17.20, page 381 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open question. Let \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) be the torus, \(T>0\) and \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\). The data are \(Z^{(N)}=(Y_i,X_i)_{i\le N}\) with \(Y_i=u_\theta(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\), where \(u_\theta=\mathscr{G}(\theta)\) solves an evolution equation with initial condition \(\theta\), the \(X_i\) are i.i.d. uniform on \(\mathcal{X}\) and the \(\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,I_W)\) are independent of them. Let \(\Pi_N\) be the exact posterior of \(\theta\), \((e_j)\) the Laplace eigenbasis of \(\Omega\) and \(S_N\) a summary statistic of the data. Generative Bayesian computation (GBC) simulates \(M\) training pairs, a parameter drawn from the prior and the summary of data drawn from the model given that parameter, trains a conditional generator \(\widehat G(s,U)\), with \(U\) a base random variable independent of everything, so that \(\operatorname{Law}(\widehat G(s,U))\) approximates \(\operatorname{Law}(\theta\mid S_N(Z)=s)\), in coefficient form \(\widehat G(s,U)=\sum_j\widehat Q_j(U_j\mid s)e_j\) with \(\widehat Q_j(\cdot\mid s)\) a learned conditional quantile function. The GBC posterior is \(\widehat\Pi_N=\operatorname{Law}\big(\widehat G(S_N(Z^{(N)}),U)\big)\) given the observed data \(Z^{(N)}\). The true conditional quantile map is \((\tau,s)\mapsto Q_j(\tau\mid s)\), the \(\tau\) quantile of the \(j\)th coefficient \(\langle\theta,e_j\rangle\) of \(\theta\) given \(S_N(Z)=s\).
The book’s transfer theorem for GBC (catalog entry bvm_for_gbc) is a \(\sqrt N\) statement: if \(\sqrt N\,\mathscr{W}_1(\widehat\Pi_N,\Pi_N)\to0\) in probability, where \(\mathscr{W}_1\) is the Wasserstein distance of order one on the negative Sobolev space \(H^{-k-2}(\Omega)\) of Nickl’s Bernstein von Mises theorem, and \(\widehat\Pi_N\) concentrates on the localization set of Nickl’s proof with bounded moments, then \(\widehat\Pi_N\) has the same Gaussian limit as the exact posterior \(\Pi_N\), together with the further conclusions about the trajectory, coverage and efficiency listed in that entry.
The book has two finite \(N\) checks, and neither is a quantification. The first is linear: the heat equation \(\partial_tu=\nu\Delta u\), \(u(0)=\theta\) on \(\Omega=[0,1]\) with \(\nu=0.01\) and \(T=1\), a fixed Gaussian prior on the initial condition (not rescaled with \(N\)), with independent coefficients on the twenty modes \(|k|\le20\) of variances \(\sigma_{0,k}^2=\rho^2\lambda_k^{-\alpha}\), \(\alpha=3\), \(\lambda_k=4\pi^2k^2\), and the exact conjugate Gaussian posterior. With the scale \(\rho\) calibrated so that the prior standard deviation at \(|k|=1\) matches the true initial condition (\(\rho=124.0\)), the largest relative discrepancy over twenty modes between the exact posterior standard deviation and the Bernstein von Mises scale with the prior precision added, \((N\iota_k+\sigma_{0,k}^{-2})^{-1/2}\), where \(\iota_k=(1-e^{-2\nu\lambda_kT})/(2\nu\lambda_kT)\) is the information per mode, is \(6.05\times10^{-3}\) at \(N=2000\), \(1.60\times10^{-3}\) at \(N=5\times10^4\) and \(7.77\times10^{-4}\) at \(N=1.3\times10^6\). The second is nonlinear: two dimensional Navier Stokes on the \(2\pi\) periodic torus with \(\nu=5\times10^{-3}\) and \(T=1\), the initial vorticity in \(D=6\) real cosine modes with an independent Gaussian prior, the truth a draw from the prior, and \(N=80\) space time points observed with noise standard deviation \(0.45\). GBC and the Laplace approximation (the Gaussian approximation of the posterior at the maximum a posteriori estimate) are scored by their Wasserstein distance to a Metropolis reference chain, in units of posterior standard deviation, and two further regimes with \(N=25\) points (a larger amplitude, and a wider posterior) were run to look for the crossover at which non Gaussianity of the posterior would favor a simulation based method over the Laplace approximation. The crossover was not found, and neither regime made the posterior measurably less Gaussian than the main run.
Quantify the non Gaussian correction for the Taylor Green problem as a function of \(A/\nu\) and \(N\), and bound \(\mathscr{W}_1(\widehat\Pi_N,\Pi_N)\) nonasymptotically in terms of the generator approximation error for the true conditional quantile map. Here the Taylor Green problem is the inverse problem for the two dimensional Navier Stokes equations \(\partial_tu+\nu Au+B[u,u]=f\), \(u(0)=\theta\), on the \(2\pi\) periodic torus, with viscosity \(\nu\), Stokes operator \(A=-\Delta\) on divergence free mean zero fields, \(B[u,v]=P[(u\cdot\nabla)v]\) (\(P\) the projection onto divergence free fields) and \(f=0\), with true initial condition \(\theta_0=u_{\rm TG}(0)\), where \(u_{\rm TG}(t,x)=A\,e^{-2\nu t}(\sin x_1\cos x_2,\,-\cos x_1\sin x_2)\) is the Taylor Green vortex of amplitude \(A\), an exact solution for \(f=0\). The book measures the ratio of the advective coupling to the viscous decay at wavenumber \(k\) in the equation linearized about this vortex as \(cA/(\nu|k|)\) with \(c\approx0.91\).
The failure of the book’s experiments to find the crossover in any regime tested says that the answer cannot be assumed, and suggests the obstruction: the error of the Laplace approximation and the bias of GBC are governed by the same curvature of the forward map, measured in posterior standard deviations, so the two do not move independently.

Open Question 17.21, page 381 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open question. Let \(\Omega=[0,1]^d\) be the torus, \(T>0\) and \(\mathcal{X}=[0,T]\times\Omega\), and let the data be \(Y_i=u_\theta(X_i)+\varepsilon_i\) at independent uniform space time points \(X_i\in\mathcal{X}\), with Gaussian noise \(\varepsilon_i\) and \(u_\theta=\mathscr{G}(\theta)\) the solution of an evolution equation with initial condition \(\theta\), the true initial condition being \(\theta_0\), as in the book’s transfer theorem for generative Bayesian computation (GBC) (catalog entry bvm_for_gbc): if the GBC posterior approximates the exact posterior with an error of smaller order than \(N^{-1/2}\) in Wasserstein distance and concentrates on the localization set of Nickl’s proof, it has the Gaussian limit of the exact posterior for the initial condition, together with the further conclusions about the trajectory, coverage and efficiency listed in that entry. This theorem and the Bernstein von Mises theorems of Nickl (2024) and of Konen and Nickl (2026) on which it rests assume deterministic dynamics without model error: every posterior draw is a solution of the equation and lies on the solution manifold \(\mathcal{M}=\{u_\theta\}\), and a trajectory generated with model error does not lie on \(\mathcal{M}\). In the state space formulation of Carlin, Polson and Stoffer (1992) the dynamics with model error are \(u_{k+1}=u_k+\Delta t\,F(u_k)+\sqrt{\Delta t}\,G\xi_k\), with time step \(\Delta t\), \(F\) the right hand side of the equation, innovations \(\xi_k\) and noise scale \(G\). The Gibbs smoother of Carlin, Polson and Stoffer is then the smoother for the initial condition problem: the forward edge \(p(u_{k+1}\mid u_k)\) is nonlinear in \(u_k\) through \(F\), the backward edge is Gaussian in \(u_k\), and a single move update samples \(u_k\) from their product. As \(G\to0\) the chain of transitions collapses to the deterministic solution map and the smoother degenerates to a sampler for \(\theta\) alone, which is the setting of Konen and Nickl (2026).
The Bayesian calibration framework of Kennedy and O’Hagan (2001), as made operational by Higdon and coauthors, runs the simulator at a design, fits a Gaussian process emulator of \(\theta\mapsto\mathscr{G}(\theta)\), adds a discrepancy process \(\delta\) and runs Markov chain Monte Carlo on \((\theta,\delta)\). The identifiability problem between \(\theta\) and \(\delta\) (Brynjarsdóttir and O’Hagan (2014); Tuo and Wu (2016)) is Condition 2E of Nickl (2024), the stability estimate \(\|\mathscr{G}(\theta)-\mathscr{G}(\theta_0)\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}\ge c\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{H^{-1}}\), in applied form: when the discrepancy can absorb a perturbation of \(\theta\), the information operator is not injective. The natural formulation is hierarchical, with \(\delta\) a Gaussian process of amplitude \(\sigma_N\to0\); for GBC it is trivial to include \(\delta\) in the simulation of the training pairs, and for the theory the admissible rate of \(\sigma_N\) is open.
Combine the transfer theorem with a discrepancy process of amplitude \(\sigma_N\) and identify the rate at which \(\sigma_N\) must tend to zero for the deterministic limit (the Gaussian limit of that theorem for dynamics without model error) to persist, connecting to the Gibbs smoother above and to the particle methods for state space models with static parameters (Storvik (2002); Carvalho, Johannes, Lopes and Polson (2010)). In the linear model without a latent state these particle systems collapse (the sufficient statistic is a deterministic function of the data, all weights are equal and there is nothing to resample), whereas with \(G\ne0\) the statistic depends on the sampled path, the weights are no longer equal, and the degeneracy of particles can occur.

title: Results by chapter On Hilbert’s 6th Problem
text:
Proposition 20.5, page 415 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. First stated in Carvalho, Johannes, Lopes and Polson (2010), Particle learning and smoothing, Statistical Science 25, 88 to 106.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider a state space model with a static parameter \(\theta\), hidden states \(x_t\) and observations \(y_t\), with the Markov structure of such a model: \(y_{t+1}\) depends on the past only through the essential state \(z_t=(x_t,s_t,\theta)\), and \(p(x_{t+1}\mid z_t,y_{1:t+1})=p(x_{t+1}\mid z_t,y_{t+1})\). Suppose there are conditional sufficient statistics \(s_t\), updated deterministically by \(s_{t+1}=S(s_t,x_t,x_{t+1},y_{t+1})\), such that \(p(\theta\mid x_{0:t},y_{1:t})=p(\theta\mid s_t)\). Particle learning updates the essential state in four steps: (1) resample \(z_t\) with weights proportional to the predictive likelihood \(p(y_{t+1}\mid z_t)=\int p(y_{t+1}\mid x_{t+1},\theta)\,p(x_{t+1}\mid x_t,\theta)\,\mathrm{d}x_{t+1}\); (2) propagate \(x_{t+1}\sim p(x_{t+1}\mid z_t,y_{t+1})\); (3) update \(s_{t+1}=S(s_t,x_t,x_{t+1},y_{t+1})\); (4) draw \(\theta\sim p(\theta\mid s_{t+1})\). Let \(z_t\) have the law \(p(z_t\mid y_{1:t})\). Reweight this law by the predictive likelihood \(p(y_{t+1}\mid z_t)\), which is step one at the level of laws, and then apply steps two to four. Then the new essential state \((x_{t+1},s_{t+1},\theta)\) has the law \(p(x_{t+1},s_{t+1},\theta\mid y_{1:t+1})\).
Source: source/chapters/ext/ch14_pl.tex, label prop:pl_exact.




Theorem 20.9, page 423 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let the input spikes \(t_k\) form a Poisson process of rate \(\lambda>0\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). Attach to the \(k\)th spike a mark \((\tau_k,\kappa_k)\), the marks being independent with a common law \(M\) on \((0,\infty)^2\) and independent of the spike times, and given the marks let the amplitude \(A_k\) be exponential with rate \(\kappa_k\). Let \(V=\sum_{t_k\le t}A_k e^{-(t-t_k)/\tau_k}\) be the stationary potential at time \(t\). Then for every \(\theta>0\), with both sides possibly equal to \(+\infty\), \(-\log\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\theta V}=\lambda\int\tau\log\big(1+\theta/\kappa\big)\,M(\mathrm{d}\tau,\mathrm{d}\kappa)=\int\log\big(1+\theta/y\big)\,U(\mathrm{d}y)\), where \(U\) is the image of the measure \(\lambda\tau\,M(\mathrm{d}\tau,\mathrm{d}\kappa)\) under \((\tau,\kappa)\mapsto\kappa\). If \(\int\log(1+1/y)\,U(\mathrm{d}y)<\infty\), which is the condition that \(U\) be a Thorin measure, then \(V\) is a generalized Gamma convolution with Thorin measure \(U\) and zero drift, that is, \(\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\theta V}=\exp\big(-\int\log(1+\theta/y)\,U(\mathrm{d}y)\big)\) for \(\theta>0\). Otherwise \(V=\infty\) almost surely. In particular, if all marks equal \((\tau,\kappa)\) then \(V\) has the Gamma law with shape \(\lambda\tau\) and rate \(\kappa\), and if \(\tau_k\) and \(\kappa_k\) are independent and \(\kappa_k\) has law \(\nu\) then \(U=\lambda\,\mathbb{E}[\tau_k]\,\nu\).
Source: source/chapters/ch14_filters.tex, label thm:shot_noise_neuron.

title: Results by chapter On Hilbert’s 6th Problem
text:
Open Problem 1, page 445 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. This is a program, and its first task is to fix the regime. Consider hard spheres in the Boltzmann Grad limit with Gibbs initial data conditioned on a macroscopic density, velocity and temperature profile, observed through the hydrodynamic fields at a later time with noise of standard deviation \(\sigma\). Find a relation between \(\sigma\), the Knudsen number and the number of particles under which the deviation of the particle fields from the solution of the limiting fluid equations is small compared with \(\sigma\), and prove under it a Bernstein von Mises theorem for smooth functionals of the initial macroscopic profile, with constants that do not depend on the number of particles.

Open Problem 2, page 445 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Give quantitative versions of the method of arbitrary functions (for a real random variable \(X\) with a density \(g\) of total variation \(V<\infty\), \(t>0\) and \(a\in[0,1]\), \(|\mathbb{P}(\{tX\}\in[0,a))-a|\le a(1-a)V/(2t)\), where \(\{\cdot\}\) is the fractional part) for mixed phase space systems such as Hénon Heiles, where invariant tori and chaotic regions coexist, with rates in terms of the measure of the chaotic sea.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:poincare.




Open Problem 3, page 445 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Quantitative estimates for chaos and entropic chaos in Kac’s model are known in several forms. Carlen, Carvalho, Le Roux, Loss and Villani (2010) relate propagation of chaos to entropy and show, in particular, that the entropic rate of convergence to equilibrium can be arbitrarily slow. Hauray and Mischler (2014) compare Kac’s chaos, entropic chaos and Fisher information chaos quantitatively, extend the estimates to measures on the Kac spheres, and treat mixtures in the sense of de Finetti, Hewitt and Savage. We do not know whether these estimates are optimal. Find the optimal rate, as a function of the marginal size \(k\) and of \(N\), in the finite de Finetti theorem for exchangeable laws on the sphere \(S^{N-1}(\sqrt N)\) in relative entropy, with examples showing that it cannot be improved, and use it to prove a propagation of chaos theorem for Kac’s model whose dependence on \(N\) is optimal under explicit hypotheses on the initial law.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:axioms.




Open Problem 4, page 445 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open problem, posed as a program in the book. Kent’s theorem writes the hitting time of a level \(b\) by a regular one dimensional diffusion, started at a reflecting or entrance boundary \(a\), as \(\sum_{n\geq1}E_n/\lambda_n\), where \(E_1,E_2,\dots\) are independent standard exponential variables and \(0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\cdots\) are the eigenvalues of minus the generator on \((a,b)\) with Dirichlet condition at \(b\) and the reflecting or entrance condition at \(a\). For each \(n\), the remainder \(\sum_{k>n}E_k/\lambda_k\) after the first \(n\) terms is a generalized Gamma convolution (a law on \([0,\infty)\) with Laplace transform \(s\mapsto e^{-\phi(s)}\), \(\phi(s)=cs+\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/y)\,U(\mathrm{d}y)\), where \(c\geq0\) and \(U\) is the Thorin measure) with an explicit Thorin measure. The problem is to identify a class of regular diffusions for which this remainder can be sampled exactly with finite expected cost, to prove that the resulting sampler is exact, and to use it to build a library of exact samplers for Brownian functionals.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:yor.




Open Problem 5, page 445 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\), \(\Xi(x)=\xi(\frac12+ix)\) and \(\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\), so that \(\Xi(x)=8\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(2xu)\,\mathrm{d}u\). The Pólya law is the law of a random variable \(X\) with the symmetric density \(\Phi(|u|)/\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(|v|)\,\mathrm{d}v\); its moment generating function is \(\mathbb{E}e^{sX}=\Xi(-is/2)/\Xi(0)\). By Khintchine’s theorem the Pólya law is the law of \(UZ\) with \(U\) uniform on \([-1,1]\) and \(Z\ge0\) independent of \(U\). The law of \(Z\) is not a generalized Gamma convolution, because \(Z\) has finite exponential moments of every order and a nonconstant generalized Gamma convolution does not. The reciprocal of the moment generating function of \(UZ\) at \(2\sqrt\lambda\) is a different matter. It is \(\Xi(0)/\Xi(i\sqrt\lambda)=\prod_n(1+\lambda/\gamma_n^2)^{-1}\), where \(\pm\gamma_n\) are the zeros of \(\Xi\), and it is the Laplace transform of a generalized Gamma convolution (a law on \([0,\infty)\) with Laplace transform \(\exp\{-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(\mathrm{d}t)\}\), \(a\ge0\), \(U\) the Thorin measure) if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds. In that case the Thorin measure is the sum of point masses at the \(\gamma_n^2\). Conversely, the logarithmic derivative of the Laplace transform of a generalized Gamma convolution is analytic outside the negative half line, which forces all the \(\gamma_n^2\) to be positive. Prove that this function is the Laplace transform of a generalized Gamma convolution by using the mixture representation \(X=UZ\) and not the location of the zeros.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:mixtures.




Open Problem 6, page 446 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. For a probability density \(u_0\) of finite variance on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) let \(u_\tau\) solve the heat equation \(\partial_\tau u=\Delta u\), and let \(W(\tau)=\tau J(u_\tau)+h(u_\tau)-\frac n2\log(4\pi\tau)-n\), where \(J(u)=\int|\nabla u|^2/u\) is the Fisher information and \(h(u)=-\int u\log u\) the differential entropy; \(W\) is nonincreasing. Ni (2004) proved that the analog of \(W\) for the linear heat equation on a Riemannian manifold is nonincreasing when the Ricci curvature is nonnegative. Extend the scale mixture proof of the monotonicity of \(W\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) (for initial densities \(u_0=\int\varphi_v\,G(\mathrm{d}v)\), mixtures of the centered Gaussian densities \(\varphi_v\) with covariance \(vI\) under a mixing law \(G\), for which \(u_\tau=\int\varphi_{v+2\tau}\,G(\mathrm{d}v)\)) to Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, interpreting the Ricci term as a correction to the subordinated Brownian motion.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:perelman.




Open Problem 7, page 446 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Formulate a prior on Nelson’s diffusions (diffusions with diffusion constant \(\hbar/2m\) whose drift is determined by the density \(\rho\) and the phase \(S\) of a wave function \(\psi=\sqrt\rho\,e^{iS/\hbar}\)) that does not itself impose the quantization condition, and identify data that determine the circulation of the drift around the nodes of the density, so that the posterior concentrates on drifts satisfying the quantization condition. Position statistics alone fix the density and, through the continuity equation, only the divergence of the current, so the data must carry more. A solution would give a Bayesian answer to Wallstrom’s objection. Wallstrom (1994) observed that the condition that \(\psi\) be single valued, which forces the quantization of angular momentum, does not follow from Nelson’s equations, which only involve \(\rho\) and \(\nabla S\); it must be added by hand.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:quantum.




Open Problem 8, page 446 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open problem. Consider the Kac walk with \(N\) particles and total collision rate \(N\): the velocities \(v=(v_1,\dots,v_N)\) lie on the sphere \(S^{N-1}(\sqrt N)=\{\sum_{i\leq N}v_i^2=N\}\), and at rate \(N\) a pair \((i,j)\) is chosen uniformly and an angle \(\theta\) uniformly on \([0,2\pi)\), and the pair is rotated by \(\theta\). Let \(\sigma_N\) be the uniform probability law on the sphere. For a probability density \(F\) with respect to \(\sigma_N\) let \(H_N(F)=\int F\log F\,\mathrm{d}\sigma_N\) be its relative entropy with respect to \(\sigma_N\), and let \(D_N(F)=-\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}H_N(F_t)\big|_{t=0}\) be the rate at which \(H_N\) decreases at time zero along the master equation of the walk, where \(F_t\) is the solution started at \(F_0=F\). For comparison, Villani’s argument gives \(D_N(F)\geq2H_N(F)/(N-1)\) for every \(F\), and Gao, Wang and Xia state in a 2026 preprint that \(2/(N-1)\) is the best constant over all \(F\). For a probability density \(f\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) let \(Z_N(f)=\int\prod_{i\leq N}f(v_i)\,\sigma_N(\mathrm{d}v)\) and \(F^f_N(v)=Z_N(f)^{-1}\prod_{i\leq N}f(v_i)\). Fix \(M>3\) and let \(\mathcal{G}_M\) be the set of bounded probability densities \(f\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) that are normal scale mixtures, \(f(v)=\int(2\pi s)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/(2s)}\,G(\mathrm{d}s)\) with a mixing law \(G\) on \([0,\infty)\) that is a generalized Gamma convolution (a law on \([0,\infty)\) with Laplace transform \(\exp(-cs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/y)\,U(\mathrm{d}y))\) for some \(c\geq0\) and some measure \(U\) on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int\log(1+1/y)\,U(\mathrm{d}y)<\infty\), the Thorin measure), and that satisfy \(\int v^2f(v)\,\mathrm{d}v=1\) and \(\int v^4f(v)\,\mathrm{d}v\leq M\). The question is whether there is \(\lambda>0\), depending only on \(M\), such that \(D_N(F^f_N)\geq\lambda H_N(F^f_N)\) for every \(N\geq2\) and every \(f\in\mathcal{G}_M\).
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:kinetic.




Open Problem 10, page 447 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Open problem. Konen and Nickl prove a functional Bernstein von Mises theorem for the posterior of the trajectory of the two dimensional Navier Stokes equations on the torus, with root \(N\) consistent prediction of future states in the supremum norm, for a Gaussian prior on the initial condition and \(N\) noisy observations at uniformly random points of space and time. The authors know of no corresponding result for sensors at fixed locations or for other priors. The problem is to determine the posterior contraction rate for the initial vorticity from noisy point observations at a fixed array of sensors and times, in terms of the number of sensors, the number of times and the noise level, and to identify the functionals of the initial vorticity that admit a Bernstein von Mises theorem. A companion question is whether the posterior of the initial vorticity can be computed in time polynomial in the data size and the dimension.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:inference.




Open Problem 11, page 447 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Fix a finite horizon and a computable blowup criterion, for example that a norm of the solution of a Galerkin truncation of the equations exceeds a threshold before the horizon. Construct a prior on initial data and forcing for three dimensional Navier Stokes and a sequence of numerical solvers such that the posterior probability of this event is consistent, that is, converges to its true value as the resolution and the amount of data increase, and quantify how the event approximates finite time blowup of the exact solution. Consistency for the blowup of the exact solution itself, under either hypothesis, would require deciding the regularity of the data near the truth, which is the regularity problem.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:blowup.




Open Problem 12, page 447 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. This is a program. At finite Reynolds number the velocity field is smooth, so a Hölder exponent has to be defined through an inertial range statement, such as the scaling \(S_p(\ell)\propto\ell^{\zeta_p}\) of the structure functions. Develop a joint posterior for the exponents \(\zeta_p\) and the inertial range from measured velocity increments, and use it to ask whether laboratory and numerical data concentrate at, above or below the exponents \(\zeta_p=p/3\) of Kolmogorov and Onsager.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:onsager.




Open Problem 13, page 448 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Consider the planted clique problem with a known clique size \(k\) in the graph \(G(n,\frac12)\). The book records that approximate message passing succeeds for \(k\ge(1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{n/e}\), and that from a suitable starting state the Metropolis process cannot find a planted clique of size \(k=n^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) in polynomial time. Take as samplers of the posterior over clique locations either Glauber dynamics on vertex sets of size \(k\), or Langevin dynamics for a continuous relaxation of the clique indicator, in both cases initialized from the prior. Determine whether such samplers have a computational phase transition at \(k=\sqrt{n/e}\), in the sense that they succeed in polynomial time above \((1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{n/e}\) and fail below \((1-\varepsilon)\sqrt{n/e}\).
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:phase_transitions.




Open Problem 14, page 448 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Prove convergence rates for generative Bayesian computation via learned Schrödinger bridges in terms of the entropic regularization, the number of simulations and the smoothness of the posterior. Rates in the sample size are known for the entropic optimal transport cost estimated from samples, by Genevay, Chizat, Bach, Cuturi and Peyré (2019) and by Mena and Niles Weed (2019). The problem concerns the learned bridge as an estimator of the posterior.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:transport.




Open Problem 15, page 448 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. The Landauer bound bounds the heat dissipated by a physical process in terms of the entropy removed, and the Sagawa Ueda inequality bounds the work in terms of the mutual information acquired. For a Bayesian update from a prior \(\mu_0\) to the posterior \(\mu_y\), prove a lower bound on the heat dissipated by any physical implementation in terms of \(\mathrm{KL}(\mu_y\|\mu_0)\) and the information erased, and compare it with the dissipation of Langevin samplers.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:thermodynamics_of_inference.




Open Problem 16, page 448 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. This is a program whose goal is the Riemann hypothesis. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\), \(\Xi(x)=\xi(\frac12+ix)\) and \(\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\big(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u}\big)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})\), so that \(\Xi(x)=8\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(2xu)\,\mathrm{d}u\). The Pólya law is the law with the symmetric density \(\Phi(|u|)/\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(|v|)\,\mathrm{d}v\); its moment generating function is \(\Xi(-is/2)/\Xi(0)\). The de Bruijn Newman constant \(\Lambda\) is the real number such that \(H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,\mathrm{d}u\) has only real zeros if and only if \(t\ge\Lambda\), and the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to \(\Lambda\le0\). A symmetric random variable \(X\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{bX^2}<\infty\) for every \(b>0\) has the Lee Yang property if \(z\mapsto\mathbb{E}e^{zX}\) has only purely imaginary zeros; the uniform law on \([-1,1]\) and the Ising spin \(\pm1\) have it. Newman’s theorem (1974): if \(X_1,\dots,X_n\) are independent with the Lee Yang property, \(J_{ij}\ge0\) are such that \(\exp(\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}x_ix_j)\) is integrable against the product law, and \(\mathbb{P}_J\) has density proportional to this exponential with respect to the product law, then \(\sum_ia_iX_i\) under \(\mathbb{P}_J\) has the Lee Yang property for every choice of positive weights \(a_i\). The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if the Pólya law has the Lee Yang property. Decide whether the Pólya law is the weak limit of a sequence of laws of random variables \(X_n\) obtained by such constructions from Ising spins and uniform laws, with \(\sup_n\mathbb{E}e^{c|X_n|}<\infty\) for every \(c>0\), which is the control that carries the Lee Yang property to the limit by Hurwitz’s theorem. A construction would prove the Riemann hypothesis, and a proof that none exists would show that this route to the hypothesis is closed.
Source: source/chapters/ch16_open.tex, label prob:bridge.

Proposition 21.4, page 433 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Hilbert’s 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Theta\) be a target and let \(M_0\) be a model with \(I(\Theta;M_0)=i_0\), where \(I\) denotes mutual information. Suppose \(M_{k+1}\) is computed from \(M_k\) and from fresh randomness independent of \(\Theta\). Then \(I(\Theta;M_k)\le i_0\) for all \(k\). If at each round the update also uses the output of a verifier \(V_k\) that depends on \(\Theta\) through a channel of capacity \(C\) bits per round, so that \(I(\Theta;V_k\mid M_k)\le C\), then \(I(\Theta;M_k)\le i_0+kC\).
Source: source/chapters/ch15_kolmogorov.tex, label prop:recursive_self_learning.

title: Clinical Trials in Practice From Foundations to AI Agents
text:
Description
Clinical trials are how medicine finds out what works, and they are slow, expensive, and tightly regulated. A well run trial can show that a treatment extends life or eases suffering. A poorly designed one can hide a real benefit, miss a serious harm, or spend years and produce nothing usable.
This book treats clinical trials as science and as regulated operations, and it gives Phase III the most room, because that is where approval is won or lost. It starts with how clinical research took its present shape, the drug development lifecycle, the regulatory frame, and the ethics of research with human subjects. It then follows a compound through the economics of development and Phases I to IV. The core of the book is the confirmatory trial: statistical foundations, adaptive and Bayesian designs, study design, real world evidence, randomization, endpoints, site selection, recruitment, logistics, data management, monitoring, safety reporting, essential documents, and the systems underneath. The closing chapters cover trial closeout, the clinical study report, and regulatory submission.
Methodology, operations, and technology are treated together. Where the book turns to automation and AI agents, one test applies: the tool must stand up in an inspection, with validation, governance, and a named person accountable for each decision.
It is written for medical directors, study managers, investigators and site staff, and for students and managers deciding whether AI has a place in regulated research.

title: On Langlands Conjectures Probabilistic Methods
text:
Description
This monograph asks what probability can contribute to the Langlands programme, and answers on two sides. The first is a limitation, proved in the opening chapter: no argument that sees only the limiting distribution of Frobenius data can detect automorphy, because equidistribution is a consequence of functoriality, not a route to it. The second is what probability does supply: consequences of the conjectures, calibration against data, and probabilistic reformulations.
The book covers Weyl’s criterion and the Sato Tate law, random matrix models of the zeros of L functions, Kloosterman sums, random class groups and Selmer groups, Hecke operators as random walks on Bruhat Tits trees, hitting times on supersingular isogeny graphs, log correlated fields, and Bayesian inference for Sato Tate groups. At its centre is the Thorin framework: for a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, the generalized Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the statement that the reciprocal of an even completion of its L function is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution. Later chapters turn the same devices on reciprocity, Fermat’s last theorem, inverse Laplace transforms, random integers and the Poisson Dirichlet law, Hecke characters and Maass forms. These are reformulations: no new case of reciprocity and no Riemann hypothesis is proved.
Results new to the book include the limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs, the Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis and for the Ramanujan conjecture, the Thorin structure of Hecke passage times, an extreme value representation of the L functions of multiplicative eta products, the Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer, and a consistency theorem for the Bayesian identification of Sato Tate groups. Open computational problems close every chapter, and the scripts and data behind the numbers are in the repository.

title: On Langlands Conjectures Probabilistic Methods
On Langlands Conjectures Probabilistic Methods
text:
Main results

Equidistribution does not determine automorphy (Proposition 1.5, page 7): Sato Tate equidistribution of a sequence indexed by the primes cannot certify that it comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) with trivial central character, because altering such a sequence on an infinite set of primes of density zero leaves the limiting empirical averages of all continuous functions unchanged but, by Ramakrishnan’s refinement of strong multiplicity one, makes it nonautomorphic, and continuum many equidistributed sequences are not automorphic.
Limit of the normalised Kemeny constants of supersingular isogeny graphs (Theorem 10.6, page 150): As the characteristic grows through primes congruent to 1 modulo 12, with the prime isogeny degree fixed, the mean time for simple random walk on a supersingular isogeny graph to hit a uniformly random curve is asymptotic to the number of vertices times the expected number of visits of simple random walk on the regular tree of the same degree to its starting point, so about twice the number of vertices for 2 isogenies.
Thorin criteria for the generalized Riemann hypothesis of automorphic L functions (Theorem 14.8, page 219): The generalized Riemann hypothesis for the L function of a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) over the rationals, and the Riemann hypothesis for zeta, are each equivalent to several positivity statements, among them that the reciprocal of the self dual completion, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure sits at the squared ordinates of the zeros, and a Hankel criterion computable from central derivatives; the theorem is an equivalence that extends the first author’s 2018 paper, and it proves no case of either hypothesis.
Thorin criterion for the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at a prime (Corollary 15.4, page 237): For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over the rationals with trivial central character, the Ramanujan Petersson conjecture at an unramified prime (outside the degenerate case of trace 2) holds exactly when the reciprocal of the symmetrised Euler factor, read in the squared variable, is the Laplace transform of a probability law, which is then a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin measure is a periodic comb (Ramanujan is local Thorin, as the generalized Riemann hypothesis is global Thorin); the corollary is an equivalence and proves no case of the conjecture.
Thorin structure of passage times of the Hecke walk on the regular tree (Theorem 15.15, page 245): The first time that continuous time simple random walk on a regular tree (the Hecke walk, on the Bruhat Tits tree when the degree is a prime plus one) reaches distance n from its start is a generalized gamma convolution whose Thorin atoms, given by the zeros of the sphere polynomials of the tree, lie in the Kesten band and follow the arcsine law as n grows, with an exact mean, a variance linear in n and a central limit theorem; Thorin support in the Kesten band is the random walk form of the Ramanujan bound, and this unconditional theorem about the tree proves no case of the Ramanujan conjecture for automorphic forms.
Gamma process limit of the Frobenius labelled factorisation of a random integer (Theorem 20.18, page 349): As the parameter of a zeta distributed random integer decreases to one, the logarithms of its prime power factors, multiplied by the parameter minus one and labelled by any equidistributed sequence of points such as Frobenius classes or Sato Tate angles, converge in law to the jumps of a standard Gamma subordinator carrying independent labels drawn from the equidistribution law, and the labelled logarithm converges in law to a Gamma random measure, so that equidistribution becomes a Gamma process.
Extreme value representation of L functions of eta products (Theorem 27.7, page 506): For every eta product, that is every product of the functions eta(m tau) raised to nonnegative integer powers r_m with the sum of m r_m equal to 24 (the thirty multiplicative eta products among them), the L function is entire and equals at every complex point the expectation of a regularised incomplete gamma function evaluated at an explicit maximum of exponential clocks, so its values at positive real points are probabilities strictly between zero and one that increase strictly to one.
Consistency of Bayes factors under equidistribution (Theorem 29.1, page 536): For any deterministic sequence, such as normalised Frobenius traces, that is equidistributed for a true law with finitely many atoms and finite Kullback Leibler divergence from one candidate law, and with a log likelihood ratio continuous off the atoms, the clipped log Bayes factor between two candidate laws is asymptotically linear in the number of observations, and as the clipping level grows its slope tends to the difference of the divergences of the true law from the two candidates, with no independence assumed.

Proposition 1.5, page 7 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be the set of primes, \(\pi(x)\) the number of primes \(p\le x\), and \(\mathbb{A}\) the adele ring of \(\mathbb{Q}\). A set \(S\subset\mathcal{P}\) has density zero if \(\#\{p\le x:p\in S\}/\pi(x)\to0\) as \(x\to\infty\). A sequence \((x_p)_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\) of real numbers comes from a cuspidal automorphic representation \(\pi\) of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A})\) with trivial central character if \(x_p=\operatorname{tr}A_p(\pi)\) for all but finitely many primes \(p\), where \(A_p(\pi)\) is the unitarily normalised Satake parameter of \(\pi\) at \(p\), and it is automorphic if it comes from some such \(\pi\); both notions are unchanged when finitely many terms are changed. A sequence \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) is equidistributed with respect to the Sato Tate law \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}(dx)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx\) on \([-2,2]\) if \(\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\phi(x_p)\to\int\phi\,d\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}\) as \(x\to\infty\) for every continuous function \(\phi\) on \([-2,2]\). Let \(\mathcal{E}\) be the set of sequences \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) that are equidistributed with respect to \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}\). (1) \(\mathcal{E}\) has the cardinality of the continuum and contains continuum many sequences no two of which agree at all but finitely many primes. The automorphic sequences fall into countably many classes under the relation of agreeing at all but finitely many primes, so all but countably many of those sequences are not automorphic. (2) Let \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) come from \(\pi\), and let \((x'_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) differ from \((x_p)\) exactly on an infinite set \(S\) of density zero. Then \((x'_p)\) is not automorphic, and \((x'_p)\in\mathcal{E}\) if and only if \((x_p)\in\mathcal{E}\).
Source: book/chapters/ch01.tex, label prop:01limits.




Corollary 1.6, page 8 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be the set of primes and \(\pi(x)\) the number of primes \(p\le x\); a set \(S\subset\mathcal{P}\) has density zero if \(\#\{p\le x:p\in S\}/\pi(x)\to0\) as \(x\to\infty\). Call a sequence \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) automorphic if there is a cuspidal automorphic representation \(\pi\) of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{A})\), where \(\mathbb{A}\) is the ring of adeles of \(\mathbb{Q}\), with trivial central character such that \(x_p=\operatorname{tr}A_p(\pi)\) for all but finitely many primes \(p\), where \(A_p(\pi)\) is the unitarily normalised Satake parameter of \(\pi\) at \(p\). Let \(\mathcal{E}\) be the set of sequences \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) that are equidistributed with respect to the Sato Tate law, that is, with \(\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\phi(x_p)\to\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-2}^{2}\phi(t)\sqrt{4-t^2}\,dt\) as \(x\to\infty\) for every continuous function \(\phi\) on \([-2,2]\). Let \(\Phi\) be any function on \([-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) that is unchanged when a sequence is altered on a set of density zero; for instance any function of the set of weak limit points of the empirical measures \(\pi(x)^{-1}\sum_{p\le x}\delta_{x_p}\) as \(x\to\infty\), which is unchanged by such alterations. Then for every automorphic \((x_p)\in[-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) there are continuum many sequences in \([-2,2]^{\mathcal{P}}\) that are not automorphic and on which \(\Phi\) takes the value it takes on \((x_p)\); if \((x_p)\in\mathcal{E}\), they all lie in \(\mathcal{E}\). In particular \(\Phi\) cannot characterise automorphy.
Source: book/chapters/ch01.tex, label cor:01functional.







Conjecture 5.3, page 67 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(E\) be an elliptic curve over \(\mathbb{Q}\) of conductor \(N\) without complex multiplication. For a prime \(p \nmid N\) put \(a_p = p + 1 - \#E(\mathbb{F}_p)\) and \(x_p = a_p/\sqrt{p} \in [-2,2]\). Let \(p_1 < p_2 < \cdots\) be the primes not dividing \(N\), let \(F_n\) be the empirical distribution function of \(x_{p_1}, \dots, x_{p_n}\), let \(F_{\mathrm{ST}}(t) = \int_{-2}^{t} \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4-u^2}\,du\) be the distribution function of the Sato Tate law on \([-2,2]\), and let \(D_n = \sup_{t \in [-2,2]} |F_n(t) - F_{\mathrm{ST}}(t)|\) be the Kolmogorov discrepancy. For \(x \ge 2\) let \(n = n(x)\) be the number of primes \(p \le x\) with \(p \nmid N\). Conjecture (open): (a) (a conjecture of Akiyama and Tanigawa) \(D_n = O(n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})\) for every \(\varepsilon > 0\); (b) \(\sqrt{n}\,D_n \to 0\) in logarithmic density, that is, for every \(\delta > 0\) the set \(S_\delta\) of real \(x \ge 2\) with \(\sqrt{n}\,D_n > \delta\) has logarithmic density zero, \(\frac{1}{\log X}\int_{S_\delta \cap [2,X]} \frac{dx}{x} \to 0\) as \(X \to \infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05.tex, label conj:05bridge.







Proposition 7.13, page 100 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(p\) be an odd prime, write \(e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}\), and for \(x\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times\) let \(\bar x\) denote its inverse. For \(t\in[0,1]\) let \(I=\{1,\dots,m\}\) with \(m=\lfloor t(p-1)\rfloor\), viewed as a set of residues modulo \(p\), let \(-I=\{p-x:x\in I\}\), and put \(R_I=\sum_{x\in I}e(\bar x/p)\) and \(G_I=\sum_{x\in I}e(x/p)\). Let \(a\) be uniform in \(\mathbb{F}_p^\times\). (1) For \(S_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in I}e\bigl((ax+\bar x)/p\bigr)\), [|S_p|2=,S_p2=.] (2) For \(S'_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in I}e\bigl((x+a\bar x)/p\bigr)\), [|S’_p|2=,S_p’2=.] In both cases the mean is \(\mathbb{E}S_p=-p^{-1/2}(p-1)^{-1}R_I\), respectively \(\mathbb{E}S'_p=-p^{-1/2}(p-1)^{-1}G_I\), which tends to \(0\) as \(p\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch06b.tex, label prop:06bsecond.




Corollary 7.14, page 101 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(p\) be an odd prime, \(e(z)=e^{2\pi iz}\), and \(\bar x\) the inverse of \(x\in\mathbb{F}_p^\times\). For \(t\in[0,1]\) let \(S'_p(a,t)=p^{-1/2}\sum_{1\le x\le\lfloor t(p-1)\rfloor}e\bigl((x+a\bar x)/p\bigr)\) with \(a\) uniform in \(\mathbb{F}_p^\times\), and write \(u_+=\max(u,0)\). As \(p\to\infty\) the variances of the real and imaginary parts of \(S'_p(a,t)\) converge to [,S’=(t+(2t-1)+)-,,S’=(t-(2t-1)+)-.] At \(t=\frac12\) the correction to the real part vanishes, so its limiting variance is \(\frac14\), and the imaginary part loses exactly \(1/\pi^2\): \(\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Im}S'_p(a,\tfrac12)\to\frac14-\frac1{\pi^2}=0.1487\).

Proposition 7.15, page 102 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((\mathrm{ST}_h)_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}\) be independent real random variables, each with the Sato Tate law, the semicircle law on \([-2,2]\) with density \(\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\). Put \(c_0(t)=t\) and \(c_h(t)=(e^{2\pi iht}-1)/(2\pi ih)\) for \(h\ne0\), and let \(K(t)=\sum_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}c_h(t)\,\mathrm{ST}_h\) for \(0\le t\le1\), the series being the limit of its symmetric partial sums over \(|h|\le H\) as \(H\to\infty\). Write \(u_+=\max(u,0)\). For \(s,t\in[0,1]\), [,K(s)=(s,t),,K(s)K(t)=(s+t-1)_+.] Consequently \(\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Re}K(t)=\frac12\bigl(t+(2t-1)_+\bigr)\), \(\mathrm{Var}\,\operatorname{Im}K(t)=\frac12\bigl(t-(2t-1)_+\bigr)\), and \(\operatorname{Re}K(t)\), \(\operatorname{Im}K(t)\) are uncorrelated. Moreover, almost surely, [K(1-t)=K(1)-(0t),] so \(\operatorname{Im}K(1-t)=\operatorname{Im}K(t)\), \(K(1)=2\operatorname{Re}K(\tfrac12)=\mathrm{ST}_0\), and \(\operatorname{Im}K(0)=\operatorname{Im}K(1)=0\).

Proposition 7.16, page 104 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((\mathrm{ST}_h)_{h\in\mathbb{Z}}\) be independent real random variables, each with the Sato Tate law, the semicircle law on \([-2,2]\) with density \(\frac1{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\), and let \(K(t)=t\,\mathrm{ST}_0+\sum_{h\ne0}\frac{e^{2\pi iht}-1}{2\pi ih}\,\mathrm{ST}_h\) for \(0\le t\le1\), the series being the limit of its symmetric partial sums. The random variable \(\operatorname{Im}K(\tfrac12)=\frac1\pi\sum_{h\ \mathrm{odd}}\mathrm{ST}_h/h\) is unbounded above and below, and for every \(M>0\), [(K()>M)e{-2M2},] the Chernoff bound of a centred Gaussian variable with the same variance \(\frac14\). More generally, every real random variable \(X=\sum_h\gamma_h\mathrm{ST}_h\) with \(\sum_h\gamma_h^2<\infty\), in particular every real linear combination of the real and imaginary parts of finitely many values of \(K\), satisfies \(\mathbb{E}e^{\lambda X}\le e^{\lambda^2\mathrm{Var}(X)/2}\) for all real \(\lambda\).

Theorem 9.1, page 134 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(q\ge2\) be an integer, let \(\mathcal{T}_q\) be the \((q+1)\) regular tree with graph distance \(d\) and a fixed vertex \(o\), let \(A\) be its adjacency operator, let \(X=q^{-1/2}A\), a bounded self adjoint operator on \(\ell^2(\mathcal{T}_q)\), and let \(\mu_q\) be the spectral measure of \(X\) at \(\delta_o\), so that \(\langle\delta_o,\phi(X)\delta_o\rangle=\int\phi\,d\mu_q\) for continuous \(\phi\). For \(n\ge0\) let \(A_n\) be the operator \(A_nf(v)=\sum_{d(v,w)=n}f(w)\), with \(A_0=I\), and put \(B_n=q^{-n/2}A_n\). Write \(U_n\) for the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind, \(U_n(\cos\theta)=\sin((n+1)\theta)/\sin\theta\), and \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}(dx)=\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx/(2\pi)\) for the Sato Tate measure on \([-2,2]\). Then: (1) \(B_1=U_1(X/2)\) and \(B_n=U_n(X/2)-q^{-1}U_{n-2}(X/2)\) for \(n\ge2\). (2) \(c_n=\int U_n(x/2)\,d\mu_q(x)\) equals \(q^{-n/2}\) for \(n\) even and \(0\) for \(n\) odd. (3) \(\mu_q\) is supported on \([-2,2]\) with the Kesten McKay density [_q(dx)=,dx .] (4) If \(S\) is simple random walk on \(\mathcal{T}_q\) started at \(o\), then \(\int x^{2m}\,d\mu_q=(q+1)^{2m}q^{-m}\,\mathbb{P}(S_{2m}=o)\) for \(m\ge0\). (5) The walk returns to \(o\) with probability \(1/q\), and the Green function \(G(1)=\sum_{n\ge0}\mathbb{P}(S_n=o)\), the expected number of visits to \(o\), equals \(q/(q-1)\). (6) \(\mu_q\) converges weakly to \(\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}\) as \(q\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch07.tex, label thm:07tree.







Proposition 10.3, page 147 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(q\ge1\) be an integer and let \(G\) be a finite connected \((q+1)\) regular graph on \(n\) vertices, possibly with loops and multiple edges, with adjacency matrix \(A\) (a loop contributing \(2\) to the diagonal) and eigenvalues \(q+1=\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n\). Its Ihara zeta function is \(Z_G(u)=\prod_{\mathfrak p}(1-u^{\nu(\mathfrak p)})^{-1}\), the product over the classes \(\mathfrak p\), under cyclic rotation, of primitive closed paths of oriented edges without backtracking and without tail, with \(\nu(\mathfrak p)\) the length; by the Ihara Bass determinant formula it is a rational function of \(u\), and its poles in \(\{\pm1,\pm1/q\}\) are called trivial. \(Z_G\) satisfies the graph Riemann hypothesis if every nontrivial pole lies on the circle \(|u|=q^{-1/2}\), and \(G\) is Ramanujan if every eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(A\) with \(|\lambda|\ne q+1\) satisfies \(|\lambda|\le2\sqrt q\). Let \(P=A/(q+1)\) be the transition matrix of simple random walk on \(G\), let \(\lambda_*=\max\{|\lambda_j|:|\lambda_j|\ne q+1\}\) (with \(\lambda_*=0\) if there is no such eigenvalue), let \(\beta=1\) if \(G\) is bipartite and \(\beta=0\) otherwise, let \(\delta_t=\max_{x}\bigl|P^t(x,x)-(1+\beta(-1)^t)/n\bigr|\), and let \(\rho_q=2\sqrt q/(q+1)\). Then the following are equivalent: (1) \(Z_G\) satisfies the graph Riemann hypothesis; (2) \(G\) is Ramanujan; (3) \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}\delta_t^{1/t}\le\rho_q\). Moreover \(\limsup_t\delta_t^{1/t}=\lambda_*/(q+1)\) exactly, so the return probabilities of a Ramanujan graph approach equilibrium at an exponential rate no slower than the rate \(\rho_q\) at which the return probabilities of simple random walk on the \((q+1)\) regular tree tend to zero.
Source: book/chapters/ch08.tex, label prop:08three.




Theorem 10.6, page 150 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\ell\) be a prime. For a prime \(N\equiv1\pmod{12}\) with \(N\ne\ell\), let \(G_N(\ell)\) be the supersingular \(\ell\) isogeny graph in characteristic \(N\), whose vertices are the \(h=(N-1)/12\) isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over \(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_N\), each curve having one edge for each of its \(\ell+1\) subgroups of order \(\ell\), joining it to the quotient curve; dual isogenies pair the edges, so that \(G_N(\ell)\) is an undirected \((\ell+1)\) regular graph, possibly with loops and multiple edges. For simple random walk \((X_t)\) on \(G_N(\ell)\), whose stationary law \(\pi\) is uniform, let \(\tau_y=\min\{t\ge0:X_t=y\}\) and let \(K_N=\sum_y\pi(y)\,\mathbb{E}_x\tau_y\) be the Kemeny constant, which does not depend on the starting vertex \(x\). As \(N\to\infty\) through primes \(N\equiv1\pmod{12}\), with \(\ell\) fixed, [.] Equivalently, the mean hitting time of a uniformly random target, from any fixed start or from a uniformly random one, is asymptotic to \(\ell h/(\ell-1)\); for \(\ell=2\) it is about \(2h\).
Source: book/chapters/ch08.tex, label thm:08kemeny.







Proposition 11.3, page 160 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta\) be the discriminant modular form of weight \(12\) and level \(1\), with Fourier coefficients \(\tau(n)\), and let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-11/2-s}\) be its \(L\) function in the unitary normalisation, with centre \(s=\tfrac12\). For every \(\sigma>1\) we have \(\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|L(\sigma+it,\Delta)|>L(\sigma,\Delta)>0\). In particular \(t\mapsto L(\sigma+it,\Delta)/L(\sigma,\Delta)\) is not a characteristic function.
Source: book/chapters/ch09.tex, label prop:ch09notcf.




Proposition 11.12, page 167 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((\theta_p)\), indexed by the primes \(p\), be independent random variables with the Sato Tate law \(\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\) on \([0,\pi]\), and let \(L_{\mathrm{rand}}(s)=\prod_p(1-e^{i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}(1-e^{-i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}\) be the Sato Tate random Euler product. For real \(\sigma>1/2\) and real \(t\) the product \(L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma+it)\), the limit of the partial products over the primes \(p\le P\) as \(P\to\infty\), converges almost surely and in \(L^2\), and [,|L_{}(+it)|^2=(2).]
Source: book/chapters/ch09.tex, label prop:ch09martingale.




Theorem 11.13, page 167 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((\theta_p)\), indexed by the primes \(p\), be independent random variables with the Sato Tate law \(\frac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\) on \([0,\pi]\), and let \(L_{\mathrm{rand}}(s)=\prod_p(1-e^{i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}(1-e^{-i\theta_p}p^{-s})^{-1}\) be the Sato Tate random Euler product; for real \(\sigma>1/2\) every factor is positive and \(\log L_{\mathrm{rand}}(\sigma)=\sum_p\sum_{k\ge1}2\cos(k\theta_p)/(kp^{k\sigma})\) converges almost surely. Let \(V(\sigma)=\sum_pp^{-2\sigma}\), so that \(V(\sigma)=\log\frac{1}{2\sigma-1}+O(1)\) as \(\sigma\to\frac12^+\). Then [N(0,1),^+,] where \(\Longrightarrow\) denotes convergence in law and \(N(0,1)\) is the standard normal law.
Source: book/chapters/ch09.tex, label thm:ch09clt.







Proposition 12.4, page 175 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f\) be a real analytic function on a neighbourhood of a compact interval \([a,b]\), with finitely many zeros \(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_r\) in \((a,b)\), all simple, and no zero at \(a\) or at \(b\). Then, as \(x\to\infty\), the Lebesgue measure of the set \(\{t\in[a,b]:\log|f(t)|<-x\}\) equals \(2e^{-x}\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{1}{|f'(\gamma_j)|}+O(e^{-2x})\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09blefttail.




Conjecture 12.6, page 178 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), be the discriminant cusp form of weight \(12\) for \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\), let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\), whose critical line is \(\operatorname{Re}s=6\), and for each prime \(p\) let \(\theta_p\in[0,\pi]\) be defined by \(\tau(p)=2p^{11/2}\cos\theta_p\). Let \(\gamma_{\mathrm E}\) be Euler’s constant and put \(A_\Delta=\sum_p\bigl(\log(1-\frac1p)+\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{(2\cos m\theta_p)^2}{m^2p^m}\bigr)\) and \(V_\Delta(T)=\frac12\bigl(\log\bigl(2\log\frac{T}{2\pi}\bigr)+\gamma_{\mathrm E}+1+A_\Delta\bigr)\). Conjecture: for \(t\) uniformly distributed on \([T,2T]\), \(\operatorname{Var}\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=V_\Delta(T)+o(1)\) as \(T\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label conj:09bvar.




Proposition 12.7, page 180 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((U_p)\), indexed by the primes, be independent random variables uniformly distributed on the unit circle, and for \(P\ge3\) and real \(h\) put \(X_P(h)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{p\le P}U_pp^{-1/2-ih}\). Then \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_P(h),X_P(h'))=\frac12\sum_{p\le P}\frac{\cos((h - h')\log p)}{p}=\frac12\log\min\bigl(\log P,\frac{1}{|h - h'|}\bigr)+O(1)\), uniformly in \(P\) and in \(0<|h - h'|\le1\). The same holds for the field \(X^\Delta_P(h)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{p\le P}\lambda(p)U_pp^{-1/2-ih}\), where \(\lambda(p)=\tau(p)/p^{11/2}\) and \(\tau(n)\) are the coefficients of the discriminant cusp form \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), with \(\lambda(p)^2/p\) in place of \(1/p\) in the sum, that is, \(\operatorname{Cov}(X^\Delta_P(h),X^\Delta_P(h'))=\frac12\sum_{p\le P}\frac{\lambda(p)^2\cos((h - h')\log p)}{p}=\frac12\log\min\bigl(\log P,\frac{1}{|h - h'|}\bigr)+O(1)\) with the same uniformity.
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09bcov.




Proposition 12.8, page 181 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(b\ge2\) be an integer and \(\sigma>0\), and let \(\{B_v(s):0\le s\le n\}\), indexed by the \(b^n\) leaves \(v\) of the \(b\) ary tree of depth \(n\), be Brownian motion indexed by the tree: each edge carries an independent Brownian path of duration one and variance \(\sigma^2\) per unit time, and \(B_v\) is the concatenation of the paths along the edges from the root to \(v\). Put \(c=\sigma\sqrt{2\log b}\), \(\theta=c/\sigma^2=\sqrt{2\log b}/\sigma\) and \(x_n=cn - a\log n\) for a constant \(a>0\). Fix \(y\ge0\). Let \(N_n(y)\) be the number of leaves with \(B_v(n)\ge x_n+y\), and \(Z_n(y)\) the number of leaves with \(B_v(n)\in[x_n+y,x_n+y+1]\) and \(B_v(s)\le\frac snx_n+y+1\) for all \(s\in[0,n]\). As \(n\to\infty\), \(\mathbb{E}N_n(y)\sim\frac{\sigma}{c\sqrt{2\pi}}\,n^{\theta a-\frac12}e^{-\theta y}\) and \(\mathbb{E}Z_n(y)\sim\kappa\,(1+y)\,n^{\theta a-\frac32}e^{-\theta y}\), with \(\kappa=2(\theta-1+e^{-\theta})/(\sigma^3\theta^2\sqrt{2\pi})\). In particular the choice \(a=\frac1{2\theta}\) makes \(\mathbb{E}N_n(y)\) of order one, while \(a=\frac3{2\theta}\) makes \(\mathbb{E}Z_n(y)\to\kappa(1+y)e^{-\theta y}\), and for that choice \(\mathbb{E}N_n(y)\) grows like \(n\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09bballot.




Proposition 12.16, page 193 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta), for the Gaussian limit only.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\), let \(W\) be a random variable with density \(\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) (the P'olya variable of \(\Delta\)), and let \(\varphi_W(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{itW}\). For real \(t\), \(\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=\log|\varphi_W(t)|-\log|\Gamma(6+it)|+\log(\Gamma(6)L(6,\Delta))\), and, as \(|t|\to\infty\), \(\log|L(6+it,\Delta)|=\log|\varphi_W(t)|+\frac\pi2|t|-\frac{11}2\log|t|+C_\Delta+O(1/|t|)\), with \(C_\Delta=\log(120\,L(6,\Delta))-\frac12\log2\pi=3.6355\). Consequently, if all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)\) lie on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=6\) (the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,\Delta)\)), then for \(t\) uniformly distributed on \([T,2T]\) the quantity \(\bigl(\log|\varphi_W(t)|+\frac\pi2t-\frac{11}2\log t+C_\Delta\bigr)/\sqrt{\frac12\log\log T}\) converges in law to the standard normal distribution as \(T\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch09b.tex, label prop:09bpolya.




Proposition 12.17, page 194 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the Riemann hypothesis for L(s, Delta).
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\); let \(W\) have density \(\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) and \(\varphi_W(t)=\mathbb{E}e^{itW}\). Assume the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,\Delta)\), so that the zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)\) are \(6\pm i\gamma_k\) with \(0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\dots\), listed with multiplicity. Let \(\tau_\Delta=\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\), and let \(Y=\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables. For real \(t\ne\pm\gamma_k\), \(\log|\varphi_W(t)|=\sum_k\log\bigl|1-\frac{t^2}{\gamma_k^2}\bigr|=\int_{(0,\infty)}\log\bigl|1-\frac{t^2}{x}\bigr|\,\tau_\Delta(dx)=-\log|\mathcal{L}_Y(t^2)|\), where \(\mathcal{L}_Y(u)=\prod_k(1-u/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}\) is the meromorphic continuation to \(\mathbb{C}\) of the moment generating function \(\mathbb{E}e^{uY}\), \(u<\gamma_1^2\). Moreover, on each interval between consecutive zeros, \(t\mapsto\log|\varphi_W(t)|\) is strictly concave.

Proposition 12.18, page 194 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E_{j,n}\), \(1\le j\le24\), \(n\ge1\), be independent standard exponential variables and \(M^*=\max_{j,n}E_{j,n}/(2\pi n)\), so that the discriminant cusp form \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), satisfies \(\Delta(iy)=e^{-2\pi y}\mathbb{P}(M^*\le y)\) for \(y>0\). Let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\), let \(G\) have the gamma law of shape \(6\) and unit rate, independent of \(M^*\), and write \(\mathbb{E}[X;A]=\mathbb{E}[X\,1_A]\) for an event \(A\). For real \(t\), \(\frac{\Gamma(6+it)}{\Gamma(6)}\,L(6+it,\Delta)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[G^{it};\,G\ge2\pi M^*\bigr]\). The finite measure \(\nu(B)=\mathbb{P}(\log G\in B,\ G\ge2\pi M^*)\) has total mass \(L(6,\Delta)\) and equals \(L(6,\Delta)\) times the law of \(W+\log2\pi\), where \(W\) is the P'olya variable of \(\Delta\), with density \(\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\).

Theorem 13.6, page 203 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), be the discriminant cusp form of weight \(12\) for \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\), let \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\), and let \(W\) be a random variable with the probability density \(\Phi_\Delta(u)=\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\), \(u\in\mathbb{R}\) (the P'olya kernel of \(\Delta\)). Then \(W\) is symmetric, has moments of all orders and an entire moment generating function, and for all \(z\in\mathbb{C}\), \(\mathbb{E}[e^{zW}]=\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\). In particular \(\mathbb{E}[e^{itW}]=\Lambda(6+it,\Delta)/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) is real and even, and the Riemann hypothesis for \(\Delta\) (all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)\) lie on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=6\)) is equivalent to the statement that the characteristic function of \(W\) has only real zeros.

Theorem 13.7, page 204 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\), and let \(W\) have density \(\Delta(ie^u)e^{6u}/\Lambda(6,\Delta)\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). Write each zero of \(z\mapsto\Lambda(6+z,\Delta)\) as \(z=i\gamma\) (no such \(z\) is real, since \(\Lambda(6+x,\Delta)>0\) for real \(x\)), and list one representative of each pair \(\{\gamma,-\gamma\}\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0\) as \(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\dots\), with multiplicity and in order of increasing real part. Consequently \(\mathbb{E}W=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}W=2\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2}\), where the right side is real because nonreal \(\gamma_k\) occur in conjugate pairs.

Theorem 13.8, page 205 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Delta(z)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\), \(L(s,\Delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)n^{-s}\) and \(\Lambda(s,\Delta)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(s,\Delta)\). A probability law on \([0,\infty)\) is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) if it is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws; equivalently (Thorin) its Laplace transform is \(\exp\bigl(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\frac st)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)\), \(s\ge0\), with drift \(a\ge0\) and a positive measure \(\tau\) on \((0,\infty)\), finite on compact sets, the Thorin measure, satisfying \(\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty\) and \(\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty\). When they hold, writing the zeros as \(6\pm i\gamma_k\) with \(\gamma_k>0\), listed with multiplicity, the GGC has drift \(0\) and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\), it is the law of \(X=\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables, and its L'evy measure has density \(k(x)/x\), where \(k(x)=\sum_ke^{-\gamma_k^2x}\), \(x>0\), is completely monotone.

Theorem 13.10, page 207 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a self dual cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge2\), with completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation, conductor included, so that \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) is entire of order one, real on the real axis, and satisfies \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon\Lambda(1-s,\pi)\) with \(\varepsilon=\pm1\). A probability law on \([0,\infty)\) is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC) if it is a weak limit of finite convolutions of gamma laws; equivalently its Laplace transform is \(\exp\bigl(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+\frac st)\,\tau(dt)\bigr)\), \(s\ge0\), with \(a\ge0\) and a positive measure \(\tau\) on \((0,\infty)\), finite on compact sets, the Thorin measure, satisfying \(\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty\) and \(\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty\). Suppose \(\Lambda(\frac12,\pi)\ne0\). Then the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(\pi\) (all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) lie on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12\)) holds if and only if \(s\mapsto\Lambda(\frac12,\pi)/\Lambda(\frac12+\sqrt s,\pi)\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC, and then its Thorin measure is \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\) over the ordinates \(\gamma_k>0\) of the zeros \(\frac12\pm i\gamma_k\).

Lemma 14.6, page 215 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist \(|\cdot|^{iy}\) of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), and let \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\gamma(s,\pi)L(s,\pi)\) be its completed \(L\) function in the unitary normalisation, in which the Dirichlet series \(L(s,\pi)=\sum_ma_\pi(m)m^{-s}\) converges absolutely for \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\) and \(\gamma(s,\pi)=N_\pi^{s/2}\prod_{j=1}^n\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\mu_j)\), with \(N_\pi\) the conductor, \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\) and archimedean parameters \(\mu_j\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\mu_j>-\frac12\); \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) is entire of order one and satisfies \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon(\pi)\Lambda(1-s,\tilde\pi)\) with \(|\varepsilon(\pi)|=1\), \(\tilde\pi\) the contragredient. Let \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\), \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\) and \(F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)/\Xi_\pi(0)\), and when \(\pi\cong\tilde\pi\) let \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)/z^r\). Then (i) \(\Xi_\pi\) is entire, even, and \(\Xi_\pi(\bar z)=\overline{\Xi_\pi(z)}\), so it is real on \(\mathbb{R}\); (ii) for real \(x\ne0\), \(\Xi_\pi(x)=|\Lambda(\frac12+x,\pi)|^2/x^{2r}\ge0\), \(\Xi_\pi(0)>0\), and \(\Xi_\pi(x)>0\) for \(|x|\ge\frac12\); (iii) \(\Xi_\pi\) has order at most one, and every zero \(z\) of \(\Xi_\pi\) satisfies \(|\operatorname{Re}z|<\frac12\); (iv) \(F_\pi\) is entire of order at most \(\frac12\) with \(F_\pi(0)=1\), and if the zeros of \(\Xi_\pi\) are listed in pairs \(\pm z_k\) with multiplicity and \(s_k=z_k^2\), then \(F_\pi(s)=\prod_k(1-s/s_k)\) with \(\sum_k|s_k|^{-1}<\infty\); (v) if \(\pi\cong\tilde\pi\) then \(\varepsilon(\pi)=(-1)^r\), and \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi\) is entire, even and real on \(\mathbb{R}\) with \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(0)\ne0\). The same statements hold for \(\Xi_\zeta(z)=\xi(\frac12+z)\), where \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)\), which is moreover strictly positive on \(\mathbb{R}\).

Theorem 14.7, page 216 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(E\) be an entire function with \(E(-z)=E(z)\), \(E(\bar z)=\overline{E(z)}\) and \(E(0)=1\), of order less than two, whose zeros lie in a strip \(|\operatorname{Re}z|\le\sigma_0\). List its zeros as pairs \(\pm z_k\) with multiplicity, put \(t_k=-z_k^2\) and \(F(s)=E(\sqrt s)=\prod_k(1+s/t_k)\). A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on \([0,\infty)\) with Laplace transform \(\exp(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,\tau(dt))\), \(s\ge0\), with drift \(a\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(\tau\), a positive measure on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty\) and \(\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty\); a Stieltjes function is a function on \((0,\infty)\) of the form \(a/s+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\sigma(dt)/(s+t)\) with \(a,b\ge0\) and \(\sigma\) a positive measure with \(\int\sigma(dt)/(1+t)<\infty\). Then \(k(x)=\sum_ke^{-t_kx}\) converges absolutely and locally uniformly on \((0,\infty)\), the sums \(S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}\), \(n\ge1\), converge absolutely and are real, and the following are equivalent. (a) Every zero of \(E\) lies on \(i\mathbb{R}\); equivalently \(t_k\in(0,\infty)\) for all \(k\). (b) \(1/F\) restricted to \((0,\infty)\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (c) \(1/F(s)=\mathbb{E}e^{-sX}\) for \(s\ge0\), where \(X=\sum_kE_k/t_k\) with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables; that is, \(1/F\) is a GGC transform with drift \(0\) and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{t_k}\). (d) \(k\) is completely monotone on \((0,\infty)\). (e) \(F\) has no zero in \((0,\infty)\) and \(F'/F\) is a Stieltjes function on \((0,\infty)\). (e’) \(E\) has no real zero, and \(\operatorname{Im}(F'/F)(s)\le0\) at every \(s\) with \(\operatorname{Im}s>0\) and \(F(s)\ne0\). (f) There is a positive measure \(\nu\) on \([0,\infty)\) with \(S_{j+1}=\int u^j\nu(du)\) for all \(j\ge0\); equivalently, the Hankel matrices \((S_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^N\) and \((S_{i+j+2})_{i,j=0}^N\) are positive semidefinite for every \(N\). When these hold, \(\nu=\sum_kt_k^{-1}\delta_{1/t_k}\), the Stieltjes function in (e) is \(\sum_k(s+t_k)^{-1}\), and the Bernstein measure of \(k\) (the positive measure \(\mu\) with \(k(x)=\int e^{-tx}\mu(dt)\)) is \(\sum_k\delta_{t_k}\).

Theorem 14.8, page 219 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist \(|\cdot|^{iy}\) of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), with contragredient \(\tilde\pi\) and completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\gamma(s,\pi)L(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation: the Dirichlet series \(L(s,\pi)=\sum_ma_\pi(m)m^{-s}\) converges absolutely for \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\), \(\gamma(s,\pi)=N_\pi^{s/2}\prod_{j=1}^n\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s+\mu_j)\) with \(N_\pi\) the conductor, \(\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\) and archimedean parameters \(\mu_j\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\mu_j>-\frac12\), and \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) is entire of order one with \(\Lambda(s,\pi)=\varepsilon(\pi)\Lambda(1-s,\tilde\pi)\), \(|\varepsilon(\pi)|=1\), so that the critical line is \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12\). Let \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\), \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\) and \(F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)/\Xi_\pi(0)\). List the zeros of \(\Xi_\pi\) as pairs \(\pm z_k\) with multiplicity, write \(z_k=i\gamma_k\), call \(t_k=-z_k^2=\gamma_k^2\) the Thorin atoms of \(\pi\), and put \(k_\pi(x)=\sum_ke^{-t_kx}\) and \(S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}\) for \(n\ge1\). A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a probability law on \([0,\infty)\) with Laplace transform \(\exp(-as-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,\tau(dt))\), \(s\ge0\), with drift \(a\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(\tau\), a positive measure on \((0,\infty)\) with \(\int_{(0,1]}|\log t|\,\tau(dt)<\infty\) and \(\int_{(1,\infty)}t^{-1}\,\tau(dt)<\infty\); a Stieltjes function is a function on \((0,\infty)\) of the form \(a/s+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\sigma(dt)/(s+t)\) with \(a,b\ge0\) and \(\sigma\) a positive measure with \(\int\sigma(dt)/(1+t)<\infty\). The following are equivalent. (a) The generalized Riemann hypothesis holds for \(\pi\), that is, all zeros of \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) lie on \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12\) (equivalently, it holds for \(\tilde\pi\)). (b) \(s\mapsto1/F_\pi(s)=\Xi_\pi(0)/\Xi_\pi(\sqrt s)\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC. (c) \(1/F_\pi\) is the Laplace transform of \(\sum_kE_k/\gamma_k^2\), with \(E_k\) independent standard exponential variables: a GGC with drift zero and Thorin measure \(\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}\). (d) The L'evy function \(k_\pi(x)=\sum_ke^{xz_k^2}\), which converges for every \(x>0\), is completely monotone on \((0,\infty)\). (e) \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) has no real zero other than \(\frac12\), and \(F_\pi'/F_\pi\) is a Stieltjes function; equivalently (Herglotz criterion) \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) has no real zero other than \(\frac12\) and \(\operatorname{Im}(F_\pi'/F_\pi)(s)\le0\) whenever \(\operatorname{Im}s>0\) and \(F_\pi(s)\ne0\). (f) \((S_{j+1})_{j\ge0}\) is a Stieltjes moment sequence; equivalently (Thorin Hankel criterion) all Hankel matrices \((S_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^N\) and \((S_{i+j+2})_{i,j=0}^N\) are positive semidefinite. The same holds for the Riemann zeta function with \(\Xi_\zeta(z)=\xi(\frac12+z)\), \(\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)\), and, when \(\pi\cong\tilde\pi\), with \(\Xi^{\mathrm{sd}}_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)/z^r\) in place of \(\Xi_\pi\), in which case every Thorin atom has half the multiplicity.

Lemma 14.12, page 221 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), with completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation, contragredient \(\tilde\pi\), \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\) and self dual completion \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\). Proposition 14.13, page 222 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On Langlands Conjectures: Probabilistic Methods, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\pi\) be a cuspidal automorphic representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})\), \(n\ge1\), with unitary central character, not a unitary twist of the trivial representation of \(\mathrm{GL}_1\), with completed \(L\) function \(\Lambda(s,\pi)\) in the unitary normalisation, contragredient \(\tilde\pi\), \(r=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\) and self dual completion \(\Xi_\pi(z)=\Lambda(\frac12+z,\pi)\Lambda(\frac12+z,\tilde\pi)/z^{2r}\). List the zeros of \(\Xi_\pi\) as pairs \(\pm i\gamma_k\) with multiplicity, let \(t_k=\gamma_k^2\) and \(S_n=\sum_kt_k^{-n}\), and let \(\Phi_\pi\) be the P'olya kernel of \(\pi\), the real even continuous function with \(\Xi_\pi(z)/\Xi_\pi(0)=\int\Phi_\pi(u)e^{zu}du\) for all complex \(z\). Suppose \(\Phi_\pi\ge0\) and let \(W_\pi\) be a random variable with density \(\Phi_\pi\) (the P'olya variable of \(\pi\)). Consequently the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(\pi\) holds if and only if the sequence \(m_j=(-1)^j(j+1)\kappa_{2j+2}(W_\pi)/(2j+2)!\), \(j\ge0\), is a Stieltjes moment sequence (the sequence of moments \(\int u^j\nu(du)\) of a positive measure \(\nu\) on \([0,\infty)\)). In particular the generalized Riemann hypothesis for \(\pi\) implies \((-1)^{n+1}\kappa_{2n}(W_\pi)>0\) for all \(n\).
